metadata.title: Phase Transitions of Best-of-Two and Best-of-Three on Stochastic Block Models

extraction_notes.note: The proof-sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal on a sketch, but rigor is not allowed on proof nodes; the two informal sketches carry no rigor field, only alternative: true on their proves edges.

Numbered displays (18),(22),(23),(34),(36) retyped from equation to claim because the text calls them 'the claim'; their nodes span only the display (environment-fact span), so the arguments are steps of the enclosing proof. (28) stays an equation.

Theorem 3.2 is proved in three places, one per property (P1)-(P3); the parts live in Definition 3.1, not in the theorem's text, so no part claims were nested and each partial proof has its own proves edge to the theorem.

The proof of Proposition 4.6 ends 'This completes the proof of \cref{thm:worst_case_3M}' although Theorem 1.4's own proof uses Proposition 4.6; the edge this \ref states is marked mention to avoid a false cycle.

Tables 1 and 2 classify the fixed points by the signs of their Jacobian eigenvalues for ranges of u; they are not extracted as nodes. Table 2's caption copies Table 1's u-ranges (2/3, 3/4), an error in the source.

Section 10 repeats the Section 4 notation sentences (delta, u, T, d^(t), delta', S) for the Best-of-two; they are recorded as also_stated_at copies of the Best-of-three definitions even though T there denotes the Best-of-two map (its formula has its own node).

Left out discussion paragraphs: 'Known techniques' and the intuitive Jacobian explanation in Section 4, the symmetry remark on T, the novelty remarks after Theorems 1.2-1.3, and the figures (vector-field plots, results diagram).

nodes.name: Pull voting (voter model)
nodes.statement: In the pull voting, at each synchronous and discrete time step, each vertex adopts the opinion of a randomly selected neighbor.

nodes.name: Hassin-Peleg consensus time bound for pull voting
nodes.statement: Hassin and Peleg~\cite{HP01} showed that the expected consensus time is $O(n^3\log n)$ for all non-bipartite graphs and for all initial opinion configurations, where $n$ is the number of vertices.
nodes.statement_short: Pull voting reaches consensus in expected $O(n^3\log n)$ steps on every non-bipartite graph.
assumptions: for all non-bipartite graphs and for all initial opinion configurations
conclusions: the expected consensus time is $O(n^3\log n)$

nodes.name: Best-of-two (two sample voting, 2-Choices)
nodes.statement: The simplest multiple-choice voting process is the {\em Best-of-two} ({\em two sample voting}, or {\em 2-Choices}), where each vertex $v\in V$ randomly samples two neighbors (with replacement) and, if both hold the same opinion, adopts it\footnote{If the graph initially involves two possible opinions, this definition matches the rule described in Abstract.}.
differentia: each vertex $v\in V$ randomly samples two neighbors (with replacement) and, if both hold the same opinion, adopts it

nodes.name: Best-of-two consensus on complete graphs (Doerr et al.)
nodes.statement: Doerr et al.~\cite{DGMSS11} showed that, for complete graphs initially involving two possible opinions, the consensus time of the Best-of-two is $O(\log n)$ with high probability\footnote{In this paper ``with high probability'' (w.h.p.) means probability at least $1-n^{-c}$ for a constant $c>0$.}.
nodes.statement_short: On complete graphs with two opinions, Best-of-two reaches consensus in $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p.
assumptions: for complete graphs initially involving two possible opinions
conclusions: the consensus time of the Best-of-two is $O(\log n)$ with high probability

nodes.name: With high probability (w.h.p.)
nodes.statement: In this paper ``with high probability'' (w.h.p.) means probability at least $1-n^{-c}$ for a constant $c>0$.

nodes.name: Best-of-three consensus time on complete graphs (Ghaffari-Lengler)
nodes.statement: For example, Ghaffari and Lengler~\cite{GL18} showed that the consensus time of the Best-of-three is $O(k\log n)$ if $k=O(n^{1/3}/\sqrt{\log n})$.
conclusions: the consensus time of the Best-of-three is $O(k\log n)$

nodes.name: Best-of-two on regular expanders (Cooper et al.)
nodes.statement: Cooper et al.~\cite{CER14} showed that, for any regular expander graph initially involving two opinions, the Best-of-two reaches consensus within $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p.~if the initial bias is $\Omega(n\lambda_2)$, where $\lambda_2$ is the second largest eigenvalue of the graph's transition matrix.
nodes.statement_short: Best-of-two on regular expanders with two opinions reaches consensus in $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p. given initial bias $\Omega(n\lambda_2)$.
assumptions: for any regular expander graph initially involving two opinions
conclusions: the Best-of-two reaches consensus within $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p.

nodes.name: Erdos-Renyi random graph G(n,p)
nodes.statement: Recall that the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enri graph $G(n,p)$ is a graph on $n$ vertices where each vertex pair is joined by an edge with probability $p$, independent of any other pairs.
differentia: each vertex pair is joined by an edge with probability $p$, independent of any other pairs

nodes.name: Phase transition of Best-of-two on core-periphery networks (Cruciani et al.)
nodes.statement: They showed that a phase transition can occur, depending on the density of edges between core and periphery vertices: Either the process reaches consensus within $O(\log n)$ steps, or remains a configuration where both opinions coexist for at least $\Omega(n)$ steps.
nodes.statement_short: Best-of-two on core-periphery networks either reaches consensus in $O(\log n)$ steps or keeps both opinions for $\Omega(n)$ steps, depending on core-periphery edge density.

nodes.name: Best-of-two on the regular stochastic block model (Cruciani et al.)
nodes.statement: Under certain assumptions including $b/a=O(n^{-0.5})$, they showed that, starting from a random initial opinion configuration, the process reaches an almost {\em clustered} configuration (e.g.~both communities are in almost consensus but the opinions are distinct) within $O(\log n)$ steps with constant probability, then stays in that configuration for at least $\Omega(n)$ steps w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: On the $(a,b)$-regular SBM with $b/a=O(n^{-0.5})$, Best-of-two from a random start reaches an almost clustered configuration and stays there $\Omega(n)$ steps.

nodes.name: Stochastic block model $G(2n,p,q)$
nodes.statement: For $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p,q\in[0,1]$ with $q\leq p$, the stochastic block model $G(2n,p,q)$ is a graph on a vertex set $V=V_1\cup V_2$, where $|V_1|=|V_2|=n$ and $V_1\cap V_2=\emptyset$. In addition, each pair $\{u,v\}$ of distinct vertices $u\in V_i$ and $v\in V_j$ forms an edge with probability $\theta$, independent of any other edges, where \begin{align*} \theta = \begin{cases} p & \text{if $i=j$},\\ q & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Two communities of size $n$; intra-community edges with probability $p$, inter-community edges with probability $q\le p$, independently.
nodes.genus: graph on a vertex set $V=V_1\cup V_2$
nodes.label: def:SBM

nodes.name: Disconnectedness of sparse SBM
nodes.statement: Note that $G(2n,p,q)$ is not connected w.h.p.~if $p=o(\log n/n)$~\cite{FK16}.
conclusions: $G(2n,p,q)$ is not connected w.h.p.

nodes.name: Density assumption $p=\omega(\log n/n)$
nodes.statement: Throughout this paper, we assume $p=\omega(\log n/n)$, in which regime each community is connected w.h.p.

nodes.name: Opinion-1 sets $A^{(t)}$
nodes.statement: Let $A^{(0)}, A^{(1)}, \ldots$ be a sequence of random vertex subsets where $A^{(t)}$ is the set of vertices of opinion $1$ at step $t$.

nodes.name: Consensus time $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)$
nodes.statement: For any $A\subseteq V$, the consensus time $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)$ is defined as \begin{align*} T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \min\left\{t\geq 0\,:\,A^{(t)}\in\{\emptyset,V\},\,A^{(0)}=A\right\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Consensus time: first step at which all vertices share one opinion, starting from opinion-1 set $A$.
also_stated_at: Here, the main quantity of interest is the {\em consensus time}, which is the number of steps required to reach consensus (i.e.~the configuration where all vertices hold the same opinion).

nodes.name: Phase transition of the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $r\mathrel{\mathop:}= \frac{q}{p}$ is a constant. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item If $r>\frac{1}{7}$, then $G(2n,p,q)$ w.h.p.~satisfies the following property: There exist two positive constants $C, C'>0$ such that \begin{align*} &\forall A\subseteq V\text{ of $\bigl||A|-|V\setminus A|\bigr|= \Omega(n)$} :\\ &\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)\leq C\left(\log\log n+\frac{\log n}{\log(np)}\right)\right] \geq 1-O\left(n^{-C'}\right). \end{align*} \item If $r<\frac{1}{7}$, then $G(2n,p,q)$ w.h.p.~satisfies the following property: There exist a set $A\subseteq V$ with $\bigl||A|-|V\setminus A|\bigr|= \Omega(n)$ and two positive constants $C, C'>0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A) \geq \exp(Cn) \right] \geq 1-O\left(n^{-C'}\right). \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$ with $r=q/p$ constant: for $r>1/7$ consensus in $O(\log\log n+\log n/\log(np))$ from any $\Omega(n)$ bias; for $r<1/7$ some $\Omega(n)$-biased start needs $\exp(\Omega(n))$ steps.
assumptions: Consider the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $r\mathrel{\mathop:}= \frac{q}{p}$ is a constant.

conclusions: $G(2n,p,q)$ w.h.p.~satisfies the following property: There exist two positive constants $C, C'>0$ such that

nodes.name: Phase transition of the Best-of-two on $G(2n,p,q)$
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-two on $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $r\mathrel{\mathop:}= \frac{q}{p}$ is a constant. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item If $r>\sqrt{5}-2$, then $G(2n,p,q)$ w.h.p.~satisfies the following property: There exist two positive constants $C, C'>0$ such that \begin{align*} &\forall A\subseteq V\text{ of $\bigl||A|-|V\setminus A|\bigr|= \Omega(n)$} :\\ &\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)\leq C\left(\log\log n+\frac{\log n}{\log(np)}\right)\right] \geq 1-O\left(n^{-C'}\right). \end{align*} \item If $r<\sqrt{5}-2$, then $G(2n,p,q)$ w.h.p.~satisfies the following property: There exist a set $A\subseteq V$ with $\bigl||A|-|V\setminus A|\bigr|= \Omega(n)$ and two positive constants $C, C'>0$ such that \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A) \geq \exp(Cn) \right] \geq 1-O\left(n^{-C'}\right). \end{align*} \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Tightness of the consensus-time upper bound
nodes.statement: Note that the upper bound $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)= O(\log\log n+\log n/\log(np))$ is tight up to a constant factor if $\log n / \log (np) \geq \log\log n$.
conclusions: the upper bound $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)= O(\log\log n+\log n/\log(np))$ is tight up to a constant factor

nodes.name: Proof of tightness via the diameter
nodes.statement: To see this, observe that there exists an $A\subseteq V$ such that $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)$ is at least half of the diameter. In addition, it is easy to see that the diameter of $G(2n,p,q)$ is $\Theta(\log n / \log (np))$ w.h.p.~\cite{FK16}.
nodes.statement_short: Diameter argument: some start needs half the diameter, and the diameter of $G(2n,p,q)$ is $\Theta(\log n/\log(np))$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Worst-case analysis of the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $p$ and $q$ are positive constants. If $\frac{q}{p}>\frac{1}{7}$, then $G(2n,p,q)$ w.h.p.~satisfies the following property: There exist two positive constants $C,C'>0$ such that \begin{align*} \forall A\subseteq V\, :\, \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)\leq C\log n \right] \geq 1-O\left(n^{-C'}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For constant $p,q$ with $q/p>1/7$, Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$ reaches consensus in $O(\log n)$ steps from every initial configuration.

nodes.name: Derivation of the Erdos-Renyi corollary
nodes.statement: Based on these theorems, an immediate but important corollary follows.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize the worst-case theorems to $p=q$, where $G(2n,p,p)$ is an Erdos-Renyi graph.

nodes.name: Fast consensus of Best-of-two and Best-of-three on $G(n,p)$
nodes.statement: For any constant $p>0$, the Best-of-two and the Best-of-three on the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph $G(n,p)$ reach consensus within $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p.~for all initial opinion configurations.
conclusions: the Best-of-two and the Best-of-three on the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph $G(n,p)$ reach consensus within $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p.~for all initial opinion configurations

nodes.name: Next-step opinion-1 set $A'$
nodes.statement: For $A\subseteq V$, let $A'$ denote the set of vertices that hold opinion $1$ in the next time step.

nodes.name: Community parts $A_i$
nodes.statement: Let $A_i\mathrel{\mathop:}= A\cap V_i$ for $A\subseteq V$ and $i=1,2$.
also_stated_at: Let $A_i \mathrel{\mathop:}= V_i\cap A$ for $A\subseteq V$ and $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: High-level proof sketch of the main results
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$, and let $A^{(0)}, A^{(1)}, \ldots$ be a sequence of random vertex subsets determined by $A^{(t+1)}\mathrel{\mathop:}= (A^{(t)})'$ for each $t\geq 0$. Consider a stochastic process ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}=(\alpha_1^{(t)}, \alpha_2^{(t)})\in [0,1]^2$ where $\alpha^{(t)}_i=|A^{(t)}\cap V_i|/n$ for $i=1,2$. Our technical result in the previous paragraph approximates the stochastic process ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}$ by the {\em deterministic} process $\mathbf{a}^{(t)}$ defined as $\mathbf{a}^{(t+1)}=H(\mathbf{a}^{(t)})$ and ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(0)}=\mathbf{a}^{(0)}$ for some function $H: [0,1]^2\to [0,1]^2$ (See \cref{eqn:H_def,fig:3M_vectorfield}). The function $H$ induces a two-dimensional dynamical system, which we call the \emph{induced dynamical system}. Using this, we obtain two results concerning ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}$. First, we show that, for any initial configuration, the process reaches one of the {\em zero areas} (a neighbor of a fixed point of $H$) within a constant number of steps. To show this, in addition to the approximation result, we used the theory of \emph{competitive dynamical systems}~\cite{HS05}. Second, we characterize the behavior of ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}$ in zero areas. The zero areas depend only on $r=q/p$, and are classified into four types using the Jacobian matrix: consensus, sink, saddle and source areas (see \cref{fig:3M_proof_sketch} for a description). In consensus areas, we show that the process reaches consensus within $O(\log \log n+\log n/\log(np))$ steps. In sink areas, we show that the process remains there for at least $2^{\Omega(n)}$ steps, and also that sink areas only appear if $r<1/7$. In saddle and source areas, we show that the process escapes from there within $O(\log n)$ steps if $p$ is a constant by using techniques of \cite{DGMSS11}. Intuitively speaking, in these two kinds of areas, there are drifts towards outside. To apply the techniques of \cite{DGMSS11}, we show that $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i|]=\Omega(n)$ in the area if $p$ is constant, which leads to our worst-case analysis result. Indeed, any previous works working on expander graphs did not investigate the worst-case due to the lack of variance estimation. These arguments also enable us to study the Best-of-two process, which implies \cref{thm:phasetransition_2C}.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate the opinion densities by a deterministic 2D induced dynamical system; reach a zero area in $O(1)$ steps via competitive-systems theory, then classify zero areas by the Jacobian (consensus, sink, saddle, source).

nodes.name: Deterministic approximation
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-three on $G(2n,p,q)$, and let $A^{(0)}, A^{(1)}, \ldots$ be a sequence of random vertex subsets determined by $A^{(t+1)}\mathrel{\mathop:}= (A^{(t)})'$ for each $t\geq 0$. Consider a stochastic process ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}=(\alpha_1^{(t)}, \alpha_2^{(t)})\in [0,1]^2$ where $\alpha^{(t)}_i=|A^{(t)}\cap V_i|/n$ for $i=1,2$. nodes.statement_short: Approximate the density process by the orbit of the induced dynamical system $H$.

nodes.name: Reach a zero area

nodes.name: Classify zero areas

nodes.name: Best-of-two
nodes.statement: These arguments also enable us to study the Best-of-two process, which implies \cref{thm:phasetransition_2C}.
nodes.statement_short: The same arguments give the Best-of-two phase transition.

nodes.name: Index set $[\ell]$
nodes.statement: For an $\ell\in \mathbbm{N}$, let $[\ell]\mathrel{\mathop:}= \{1,2,\ldots, \ell\}$.

nodes.name: Neighborhood $N(v)$
nodes.statement: For a graph $G=(V,E)$ and $v\in V$, let $N(v)$ be the set of vertices adjacent to $v$.

nodes.name: Degree $\deg(v)$
nodes.statement: Denote the degree of $v\in V$ by $\deg(v)=|N(v)|$.

nodes.name: Degree into a set $\deg_S(v)$
nodes.statement: For $v\in V$ and $S\subseteq V$, let $\deg_S(v)=|S\cap N(v)|$.

nodes.name: Best-of-three voting process
nodes.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph where each vertex holds an opinion from~$\{1,2\}$. Let \begin{align*} f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \binom{3}{3}x^3+\binom{3}{2}x^2(1-x)=3x^2-2x^3. \end{align*} For the set $A$ of vertices holding opinion $1$, let $A'$ denote the set of vertices that hold opinion $1$ after an update. In the Best-of-three, $A'= \{v\in V: X_v=1\}$ where $(X_v)_{v\in V}$ are independent binary random variables satisfying \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[X_v=1]= f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Each vertex independently adopts opinion 1 with probability $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(\deg_A(v)/\deg(v))$, $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x)=3x^2-2x^3$.
also_stated_at: Likewise, the {\em Best-of-three} (a.k.a.~{\em 3-Majority}) is another simple multiple-choice voting process where each vertex adopts the majority opinion among those of three randomly selected neighbors.

nodes.name: Voting Markov chain $(A^{(t)})$
nodes.statement: For a given vertex subset $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$, we are interested in the behavior of the Markov chain $(A^{(t)})_{t=0}^{\infty}$, i.e.~the sequence of random vertex subsets determined by $A^{(t+1)}\mathrel{\mathop:}= (A^{(t)})'$ for each $t\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Concentration of $|A_i'|$
nodes.statement: \left||A'_i|-\mathbf{E}[|A_i'|]\right|=O(\sqrt{n\log n}).
nodes.statement_short: Each $|A'_i|$ is within $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$ of its mean w.h.p. (Hoeffding).
nodes.label: eqn:A'concentration

nodes.name: $f$-good stochastic block model
nodes.statement: For a given function $f:[0,1]\to [0,1]$, we say $G(2n,p,q)$ is $f$-good if $G(2n,p,q)$ satisfies the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm (P\arabic*)}] \setlength{\itemsep}{-1.8pt} \item It is connected and non-bipartite. \item A positive constant $C_1$ exists such that, for all $A, S\subseteq V$ and $i\in\{1,2\}$, \begin{align*} \left| \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}f\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) - |S\cap V_i|f\left( \frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)} \right) \right| \leq C_1\sqrt{\frac{n}{p}}. \end{align*} \item A positive constant $C_2$ exists such that, for all $A\subseteq V$, $S\in\{A, V\setminus A, V\}$ and $i\in\{1,2\}$, \begin{align*} \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}f\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) \leq |S\cap V_i|f\left( \frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)} \right) + C_2|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}. \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $G(2n,p,q)$ is $f$-good if connected non-bipartite and sums of $f(\deg_A(v)/\deg(v))$ over vertex sets match their idealized values up to $O(\sqrt{n/p})$ (P2) and $O(|A|\sqrt{\log n/(np)})$ (P3).
nodes.section: 3 Concentration result for the stochastic block model

nodes.name: Main technical theorem ($f$-goodness of SBM)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $f:[0,1]\to [0,1]$ is a polynomial function with constant degree, $p=\omega(\log n/n)$ and $q\geq \log n/n^2$. Then $G(2n,p,q)$ is $f$-good w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: For polynomial $f$ of constant degree, $p=\omega(\log n/n)$ and $q\ge\log n/n^2$, $G(2n,p,q)$ is $f$-good w.h.p.
nodes.section: 3 Concentration result for the stochastic block model
assumptions: $f:[0,1]\to [0,1]$ is a polynomial function with constant degree
conclusions: $G(2n,p,q)$ is $f$-good w.h.p.
nodes.label: thm:fgood

nodes.statement_short: Connectivity and non-bipartiteness follow from standard random-graph facts since $p=\omega(\log n/n)$ and $q\ge\log n/n^2$.

nodes.name: Idea of the proof of the main technical theorem
nodes.statement: We consider the property \ref{pro:gomiN}. Note that we may assume $f(x)=x^k$ for some constant $k$ w.l.o.g.~since it suffices to obtain the concentration result for each term of $f$. For simplicity, let us exemplify our idea on the special case of $k=3$. It is known that $\deg(v)=n(p+q)\pm O(\sqrt{np\log n})$ holds for all $v\in V$ w.h.p.~(see, e.g.~\cite{FK16}). This implies that $\sum_{v\in S}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)^3 = \frac{1\pm O(\sqrt{\log n/np})}{(n(p+q))^3}\cdot \sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3$ holds for all $S,A\subseteq V$. Indeed, it is not difficult to see that the term $O(\sqrt{\log n/np})$ can be improved to $O(\sqrt{1/np})$ (see \cref{sec:reduction}). The core of the proof is the concentration of $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3$. Note that $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{a\in A}\mathbbm{1}_{\{s,a\}\in E}$ counts the number of cut edges between $S$ and $A$. For fixed $S$ and $A$, the Chernoff bound yields the concentration of it since each edge appears independently. Similarly, the summation $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{a,b,c\in A}\mathbbm{1}_{\{v,a\},\{v,b\},\{v,c\}\in E}$ counts the number of ``crossing stars" between $S$ and $A$. However, the Chernoff bound does not work here due to the dependency of the appearance of crossing stars. Fortunately, we can obtain a strong lower bound using the Janson inequality (\cref{lem:Janson}) as follows: For $S,A,B,C\subseteq V$, let $W(S;A,B,C)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)\deg_B(v)\deg_C(v)$. From the Janson inequality and the union bound on $S,A,B,C\subseteq V$, we can show that $W(S;A,B,C)\geq \mathbf{E}[W(S;A,B,C)]-O(n^{3.5}p^{2.5})$ holds for all $S,A,B,C\subseteq V$ w.h.p. On the other hand, it is easy to check that \begin{align*} W(S;A,B,C) &= W(V;V,V,V) - W(V;V,V,V\setminus C) - W(V;V,V\setminus B,C) \\ & \ \ \ - W(V;V\setminus A,B,C)-W(V\setminus S;A,B,C). \end{align*} The Kim-Vu concentration (\cref{lem:Kim-Vu}) yields $W(V;V,V,V)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(V;V,V,V)] + O(n^{3.5}p^{2.5})$ since we do not consider the union bound here. For the other terms, we apply the lower bound by the Janson inequality. Then, we have a strong concentration result that $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3 = W(S;A,A,A) = \mathbf{E}[W(S;A,A,A)] \pm O(n^{3.5}p^{2.5})$ holds for all $S,A\subseteq V$ w.h.p. Finally, we estimate the gap between $\mathbf{E}[W(S\cap V_i,A,A,A)]$ and $|S\cap V_i|(|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q)^3$. See \cref{sec:randomgraphs} for details.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to monomials $f(x)=x^k$; bound crossing-star counts $W(S;A,B,C)$ from below by Janson's inequality with a union bound and from above by inclusion-exclusion plus Kim-Vu.
nodes.section: 3 Concentration result for the stochastic block model

nodes.name: Degree concentration
nodes.statement: It is known that $\deg(v)=n(p+q)\pm O(\sqrt{np\log n})$ holds for all $v\in V$ w.h.p.~(see, e.g.~\cite{FK16}). This implies that $\sum_{v\in S}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)^3 = \frac{1\pm O(\sqrt{\log n/np})}{(n(p+q))^3}\cdot \sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3$ holds for all $S,A\subseteq V$. Indeed, it is not difficult to see that the term $O(\sqrt{\log n/np})$ can be improved to $O(\sqrt{1/np})$ (see \cref{sec:reduction}).
nodes.statement_short: Degree concentration reduces the sum to $\sum_v \deg_A(v)^3$.

nodes.name: Crossing stars
nodes.statement: The core of the proof is the concentration of $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3$. Note that $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{a\in A}\mathbbm{1}_{\{s,a\}\in E}$ counts the number of cut edges between $S$ and $A$. For fixed $S$ and $A$, the Chernoff bound yields the concentration of it since each edge appears independently. Similarly, the summation $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{a,b,c\in A}\mathbbm{1}_{\{v,a\},\{v,b\},\{v,c\}\in E}$ counts the number of ``crossing stars" between $S$ and $A$. However, the Chernoff bound does not work here due to the dependency of the appearance of crossing stars.
nodes.statement_short: The sum counts crossing stars, whose dependencies defeat Chernoff.

nodes.name: Janson lower bound
nodes.statement: Fortunately, we can obtain a strong lower bound using the Janson inequality (\cref{lem:Janson}) as follows: For $S,A,B,C\subseteq V$, let $W(S;A,B,C)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)\deg_B(v)\deg_C(v)$. From the Janson inequality and the union bound on $S,A,B,C\subseteq V$, we can show that $W(S;A,B,C)\geq \mathbf{E}[W(S;A,B,C)]-O(n^{3.5}p^{2.5})$ holds for all $S,A,B,C\subseteq V$ w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Janson's inequality with a union bound gives a uniform lower bound on $W(S;A,B,C)$.
nodes.section: 3 Concentration result for the stochastic block model

nodes.name: Kim-Vu upper bound
nodes.statement: On the other hand, it is easy to check that \begin{align*} W(S;A,B,C) &= W(V;V,V,V) - W(V;V,V,V\setminus C) - W(V;V,V\setminus B,C) \\ & \ \ \ - W(V;V\setminus A,B,C)-W(V\setminus S;A,B,C). \end{align*} The Kim-Vu concentration (\cref{lem:Kim-Vu}) yields $W(V;V,V,V)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(V;V,V,V)] + O(n^{3.5}p^{2.5})$ since we do not consider the union bound here. For the other terms, we apply the lower bound by the Janson inequality. Then, we have a strong concentration result that $\sum_{v\in S}\deg_A(v)^3 = W(S;A,A,A) = \mathbf{E}[W(S;A,A,A)] \pm O(n^{3.5}p^{2.5})$ holds for all $S,A\subseteq V$ w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Inclusion-exclusion plus Kim-Vu for $W(V;V,V,V)$ give the matching upper bound.
nodes.section: 3 Concentration result for the stochastic block model

nodes.name: Compare with the ideal value
nodes.statement: Finally, we estimate the gap between $\mathbf{E}[W(S\cap V_i,A,A,A)]$ and $|S\cap V_i|(|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q)^3$. See \cref{sec:randomgraphs} for details.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the gap between $\mathbf{E}[W]$ and the ideal value.

nodes.statement: Throughout this paper, we use ${\boldsymbol \alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$ and ${\boldsymbol \alpha}'=(\alpha'_1,\alpha'_2)$ as vector-valued random variables.

nodes.name: Approximation by the induced dynamical system (Best-of-three)
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-three on an $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$, starting with the vertex set $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$ holding opinion $1$. Let $({\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)})_{t=0}^{\infty}$ be a stochastic process given by ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}=(\alpha^{(t)}_1,\alpha^{(t)}_2)$ and $\alpha^{(t)}_i=|A^{(t)}\cap V_i|/n$. Let $H$ be the mapping \cref{eqn:H_def} and define $(\mathbf{a}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$ as \begin{align} \begin{cases} \mathbf{a}^{(0)}={\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(0)},\\ \mathbf{a}^{(t+1)}=H(\mathbf{a}^{(t)}). \end{cases} \end{align} Then there exists a positive constant $C>0$ such that \begin{align*} \forall 0\leq t\leq n^{o(1)},\forall A^{(0)}\subseteq V\,:\,\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}-\mathbf{a}^{(t)}\|_\infty \leq C^t \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)\right] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Region $S$
nodes.statement: In \cref{lem:3Mvector_field_lem1}, we assert that the sequence $(\mathbf{d}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$ is closed in \begin{align*} S\mathrel{\mathop:}= \{(d_1,d_2)\in[0,1]^2:d_1+d_2\leq 1\}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Fixed points of the Best-of-three map $T$
nodes.statement: A straightforward calculation shows that $\mathbf{d}'=\mathbf{d}\in S$ if and only if $\mathbf{d}\in\{\mathbf{d}^*_1,\mathbf{d}^*_2,\mathbf{d}^*_3,\mathbf{d}^*_4\}$, where \begin{align} \mathbf{d}^*_i \mathrel{\mathop:}= \begin{cases} (0,0) & \text{if $i=1$},\\ \left(\sqrt{\frac{3u-2}{u^3}},0\right) & \text{if $i=2$ and $u\geq\frac{2}{3}$},\\ \left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{4u^3}},\sqrt{\frac{4u-3}{4u}} \right) & \text{if $i=3$ and $u\geq\frac{3}{4}$},\\ (0,1) & \text{if $i=4$}. \end{cases} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The fixed points of $T$ in $S$ are exactly $\mathbf{d}^*_1,\dots,\mathbf{d}^*_4$ (with $\mathbf{d}^*_2,\mathbf{d}^*_3$ existing only for $u\ge2/3$, $u\ge3/4$).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: If $r>\frac{1}{7}$ and $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$ satisfies $\bigl| |A^{(0)}|-n \bigr| = \Omega(n)$, then we have $|d^{(0)}_2|=|\delta^{(0)}_2|>\kappa$ for some constant $\kappa>0$. Next, for any constant $\epsilon>0$, \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield} implies $\absp{\mathbf{d}^{(l)}} \in B(\mathbf{d}^*_4,\epsilon)$ for some constant $l=l(\epsilon)$. From \cref{eqn:delta_d_diff}, we have $\absp{{\boldsymbol \delta}^{(l)}}\in B(\mathbf{d}^*_4,\epsilon)$ for sufficiently large $n$. Set $\epsilon$ be the constant mentioned in \cref{prop:fastconsensus_3M}. Then, from \cref{prop:fastconsensus_3M}, it holds w.h.p.~that $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(0)}) \leq l+T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(l)}) \leq O(\log\log n+\log n/\log (np))$. If $r<\frac{1}{7}$, \cref{prop:sink_3M} yields $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(0)}) \geq \exp(\Omega(n))$ w.h.p.~for any $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$ with ${\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)} \in B(\mathbf{d}^*_2,\epsilon)$, where $\epsilon>0$ is the constant from \cref{prop:sink_3M}. This completes the proof of \ref{state:belowthroshold_3M}.
nodes.statement_short: Above threshold: orbit convergence brings the process near consensus in $O(1)$ steps, then fast consensus; below: start near the sink $\mathbf{d}^*_2$.

nodes.name: Case $r>1/7$
nodes.statement: If $r>\frac{1}{7}$ and $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$ satisfies $\bigl| |A^{(0)}|-n \bigr| = \Omega(n)$, then we have $|d^{(0)}_2|=|\delta^{(0)}_2|>\kappa$ for some constant $\kappa>0$. Next, for any constant $\epsilon>0$, \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield} implies $\absp{\mathbf{d}^{(l)}} \in B(\mathbf{d}^*_4,\epsilon)$ for some constant $l=l(\epsilon)$. From \cref{eqn:delta_d_diff}, we have $\absp{{\boldsymbol \delta}^{(l)}}\in B(\mathbf{d}^*_4,\epsilon)$ for sufficiently large $n$. Set $\epsilon$ be the constant mentioned in \cref{prop:fastconsensus_3M}. Then, from \cref{prop:fastconsensus_3M}, it holds w.h.p.~that $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(0)}) \leq l+T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(l)}) \leq O(\log\log n+\log n/\log (np))$.

This completes the proof of \ref{state:belowthroshold_3M}.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.4

Then, from \cref{thm:phasetransition_3M}, we have $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(\tau)})\leq O(\log\log n+\log n/\log (np))$. Thus, $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(0)})\leq \tau + T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A^{(\tau)}) \leq O(\log n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Escape from the balanced area in $O(\log n)$ steps, then apply the phase-transition bound.

nodes.name: Escape step
nodes.statement: If $|\delta^{(0)}|=o(1)$, then \cref{prop:escape_3M} yields that $|\delta^{(\tau)}|>\kappa$ for some constant $\kappa>0$ and some $\tau=O(\log n)$.

nodes.statement_short: From a biased state consensus follows in $O(\log\log n+\log n/\log(np))$ steps.

nodes.name: $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process
nodes.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph where each vertex holds an opinion from $\{1,2\}$. Let $f_1,f_2: [0,1]\to [0,1]$ be polynomials. For the set $A$ of vertices with opinion $1$, let $A'$ denote the set of vertices with opinion $1$ after an update. In the $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process, $A'= \{v\in V: X_v=1\}$ where $(X_v)_{v\in V}$ are independent binary random variables satisfying \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[X_v=1]&= \begin{cases} f_1\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) &(\textrm{$v\in A$, i.e.~$v$ has opinion $1$})\\ f_2\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) &(\textrm{$v\in V\setminus A$, i.e.~$v$ has opinion $2$}) \end{cases}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A vertex of opinion $i$ adopts opinion 1 independently with probability $f_i(\deg_A(v)/\deg(v))$ for polynomials $f_1,f_2$.

nodes.name: Best-of-two and Best-of-three as polynomial voting processes
nodes.statement: Polynomial voting process includes several known voting models including the Best-of-two, the Best-of-three, and so on. For example, $f_1(x)=f_2(x)=f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x)=3x^2-2x^3$ for the Best-of-three. For the Best-of-two, $f_1(x)=2x(1-x)$ and $f_2(x)=x^2$.

nodes.name: Approximation by the induced dynamical system for polynomial voting processes
nodes.statement: Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be polynomials with constant degree. Consider an $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process, on an $f_1$-good and $f_2$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ starting with vertex set $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$ of opinion $1$. Let $(A^{(t)})_{t=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of random vertex subsets defined by $A^{(t+1)}\mathrel{\mathop:}= (A^{(t)})'$ for each $t\geq 0$. Let $({\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)})_{t=0}^{\infty}$, where ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}=(\alpha^{(t)}_1,\alpha^{(t)}_2)$ and $\alpha^{(t)}_i=|A^{(t)}\cap V_i|/n$. Define a mapping $H=(H_1,H_2)$ as \begin{align*} H_i(a_1,a_2)=a_i f_1\left(\frac{a_i+ra_{3-i}}{1+r}\right) + (1-a_i) f_2\left(\frac{a_i+ra_{3-i}}{1+r}\right) \,\,\,\text{for $i=1,2$}. \end{align*} Define $(\mathbf{a}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$ as $\mathbf{a}^{(0)}={\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(0)}$ and $\mathbf{a}^{(t+1)}=H(\mathbf{a}^{(t)})$ for each $t\geq 0$. Then, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \begin{align*} \forall 0\leq t\leq n^{o(1)},\forall A^{(0)}\subseteq V\,:\,\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}-\mathbf{a}^{(t)}\|_\infty \leq C^t \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)\right] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For any $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process on an $f_1$- and $f_2$-good SBM, densities track the orbit of the induced map $H$ within $C^t(1/\sqrt{np}+\sqrt{\log n/n})$ for $t\le n^{o(1)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.2
nodes.statement: For any polynomial voting process, the cardinality $|A_i'|$ can be written as the sum of independent random variables: \begin{align*} |A_i'|=\sum_{v\in V_i}X_v. \end{align*} Thus, if we fix $A\subseteq V$, the Hoeffding bound (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}) implies that \cref{eqn:A'concentration} holds w.h.p. Since \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A_i'|] &=\sum_{v\in V_i}\mathbf{E}[X_v] =\sum_{v\in A_i}f_1\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)+\sum_{v\in V\setminus A_i}f_2\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right), \end{align*} the property~\ref{pro:gomiN} and \cref{eqn:A'concentration} lead to \begin{align*} \| {\boldsymbol \alpha'}- H({\boldsymbol \alpha}) \|_\infty \leq C_1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right) \end{align*} for some constant $C_1>0$. Note that the function $H$ satisfies the Lipschitz condition. Hence, a positive constant $C_2$ exists such that \begin{align*} \|H(\mathbf{x})-H(\mathbf{y})\|_\infty \leq C_2 \|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty \end{align*} holds for any $\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\in[0,1]^2$ (see \cref{sec:lipschitzcondition}). Let ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}=(\alpha^{(t)}_1,\alpha^{(t)}_2)$ be the vector-valued stochastic process and $\mathbf{a}^{(t)}=(\mathbf{a}^{(t)}_1,\mathbf{a}^{(t)}_2)$ be the vector sequence given in \cref{eqn:veca_def}. Then, we have \begin{align*} \|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}-\mathbf{a}^{(t)}\|_\infty&= \|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)} - H({\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t-1)}) + H({\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t-1)}) - H(\mathbf{a}^{(t-1)}) \|_\infty \\ &\leq \|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)} - H({\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t-1)}) \|_\infty + C_2\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t-1)} - \mathbf{a}^{(t-1)} \|_\infty \\ &\leq C_2\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t-1)} - \mathbf{a}^{(t-1)} \|_\infty + C_1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right) \\ &\leq C^t\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right), \end{align*} where $C$ is sufficiently large constant.
nodes.statement_short: One-step error bound from Hoeffding and (P2), then propagate the error with the Lipschitz constant of $H$ by induction on $t$.

nodes.name: Error propagation

nodes.name: Jacobian matrix
nodes.statement: Recall that, the Jacobian matrix $J$ of a function $H:\mathbf{x} \mapsto (H_1(\mathbf{x}),H_2(\mathbf{x}))$ at $\mathbf{a}\in \mathbb{R}^2$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix given by \begin{align*} J= \left(\frac{\partial H_i}{\partial x_j}(\mathbf{a})\right)_{i,j\in [2]}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Sink point
nodes.statement: Consider a dynamical system $H$. A fixed point $\mathbf{a}^*\in\mathbb{R}^2$ is \emph{sink} if the Jacobian matrix $J$ at $\mathbf{a}^*$ satisfies $\sigma_{\max}<1$, where $\sigma_{\max}$ is the largest singular value of $J$.

nodes.name: Stationary dynamics around a sink point
nodes.statement: Consider an $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process on an $f_1$-good and $f_2$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $r=\frac{q}{p}$ is a constant. Let $H$ be the induced dynamical system. Then, for any sink point $\mathbf{a}^*$ and any sufficiently small $\epsilon=\omega(\sqrt{1/np})$, \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[{\boldsymbol \alpha}'\not\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon)\,\middle|\,{\boldsymbol \alpha}\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon)\right]\leq \exp(-\Omega(\epsilon^2 n)) \end{align*} holds. In particular, let \begin{align*} \tau:=\inf\left\{t\in\mathbb{N}:{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}\not\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon)\right\} \end{align*} be a stopping time. Then, $\tau\geq\exp(\Omega(\epsilon^2 n))$ holds w.h.p.~conditioned on ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(0)}\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon)$ for any $\epsilon$ satisfying $\epsilon=\omega(\max\{1/\sqrt{np},\sqrt{\log n/n}\})$.
nodes.statement_short: Near a sink point of the induced map, the process leaves an $\epsilon$-ball with probability $\exp(-\Omega(\epsilon^2 n))$, so it stays $\exp(\Omega(\epsilon^2 n))$ steps.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ at a fixed point
nodes.statement: Let $J$ be the Jacobian matrix of $H$ at $\mathbf{a}^*$ and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ be its eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Eigenvectors $\mathbf{u}_i$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{u}_i$ be the eigenvector of $J$ corresponding to $\lambda_i$.

nodes.name: Diagonalization $J=U^{-1}\Lambda U$
nodes.statement: Then, we can rewrite $J$ as \begin{align*} J=U^{-1}\Lambda U, \end{align*} where $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ and $U=(\mathbf{u}_1\,\mathbf{u}_2)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Eigen-coordinates ${\boldsymbol \beta}$
nodes.statement: For a fixed point $\mathbf{a}^* \in \mathbb{R}^2$, let ${\boldsymbol \beta}=(\beta_1,\beta_2)$ be a vector-valued random variable defined as \begin{align} {\boldsymbol \beta}=U({\boldsymbol \alpha}-\mathbf{a}^*). \end{align}

nodes.name: Definition of ${\boldsymbol \beta}$
nodes.statement: {\boldsymbol \beta}=U({\boldsymbol \alpha}-\mathbf{a}^*).
nodes.label: eqn:betadef

nodes.name: Basic assumptions (A1)-(A3)
nodes.statement: We consider an $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process on an $f_1$-good and $f_2$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ for constants $p\geq q\geq 0$. Let $\mathbf{a}^*$ be a fixed point and $J$ be the corresponding Jacobian matrix satisfying \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm (A\arabic*)}] \item The eigenvectors $\mathbf{u}_1$ and $\mathbf{u}_2$ are linearly independent. \item A positive constant $\epsilon_0$ exists such that $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha'_i\mid A]\geq \Omega(n^{-1})$ for all $i\in\{1,2\}$ and all $A\subseteq V$ of ${\boldsymbol \alpha}\in B\left(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon_0\right)$. \item The matrix $J$ contains an eigenvalue $\lambda$ satisfying $|\lambda|>1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Constant $p\ge q$; at the fixed point the eigenvectors are independent, the one-step variance is $\Omega(1/n)$ nearby, and some eigenvalue exceeds 1 in modulus.
nodes.label: asm:escape_assumption0

nodes.name: Assumptions (A4)-(A5)
nodes.statement: In addition to \cref{asm:escape_assumption0}, we assume that there exists a positive constant $\epsilon^*$ satisfying the followings: \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm (A\arabic*)}] \setcounter{enumi}{3} \item There exist two positive constants $\epsilon_1,C$ such that \begin{align*} |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i\mid A]|\geq (1+\epsilon_1)|\beta_i|-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}} \end{align*} holds for any $A\subseteq V$ of $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|\leq \epsilon^*$ and any $i\in[2]$ of $|\lambda_i|>1$. \item For any $i\in [2]$ of $|\lambda_i|\leq 1$, \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[|\beta'_i|\leq \epsilon^*\mid |\beta_i|\leq \epsilon^*] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Expanding directions grow by a factor $1+\epsilon_1$ in expectation; non-expanding directions stay bounded w.h.p.
nodes.label: asm:escape_assumption1

nodes.name: Assumption (A6): no eigenvalue of modulus one
nodes.statement: In addition to \cref{asm:escape_assumption0}, we assume the following: \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm (A\arabic*)}] \setcounter{enumi}{5} \item The eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ of $J$ satisfies $|\lambda_i|\neq 1$ for all $i\in[2]$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: asm:escape_assumption2

nodes.name: Escape from source and sink areas
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{a}^*$ be a fixed point satisfying either \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}~or~\ref{asm:escape_assumption2}. Then, there exist $\tau=O(\log n)$ and a constant $\epsilon'>0$ such that the followings hold w.h.p.: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $\|\beta^{(\tau)}\|_\infty > \epsilon'$, and \item $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j| \leq \epsilon'$ for any $j\in [2]$ of $|\lambda_j|\leq 1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Under Assumption 7.6 or 7.7 the process leaves a constant neighborhood of the fixed point along the expanding directions within $O(\log n)$ steps w.h.p.
assumptions: Let $\mathbf{a}^*$ be a fixed point satisfying either \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}~or~\ref{asm:escape_assumption2}.
conclusions: there exist $\tau=O(\log n)$ and a constant $\epsilon'>0$ such that the followings hold w.h.p.:
nodes.label: prop:escape

nodes.name: Jacobian of the Best-of-three map $T$
nodes.statement: J&=\frac{3}{2}\left( \begin{array}{cc} u(1-(ud_1)^2-d_2^2) & -2ud_1d_2 \\ -2u^2d_1d_2 & 1-(ud_1)^2-d_2^2 \end{array} \right).
nodes.label: eqn:general_Jacobian_3M

nodes.name: Jacobians $J_i$ at the fixed points
nodes.statement: Let $J_i$ be the Jacobian matrix at $\mathbf{d}^*_i$, where $\mathbf{d}^*_i$ is the fixed points \cref{eqn:fixed_points_3M}.
also_stated_at: Let $J_i$ be the Jacobian matrix at $\mathbf{d}^*_i$.

nodes.name: Jacobians at the Best-of-three fixed points
nodes.statement: J_i&=\begin{cases} \frac{3}{2}\left( \begin{array}{cc} u & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \right) & \text{if $i=1$}, \\ 3\left( \begin{array}{cc} 1-u & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{u}-1 \end{array} \right) & \text{if $i=2$ and $u\geq \frac{2}{3}$}, \\ \frac{1}{2}\left( \begin{array}{cc} 1 & -\frac{\sqrt{4u-3}}{u} \\ -\sqrt{4u-3} & \frac{1}{u} \end{array} \right) & \text{if $i=3$ and $u\geq \frac{3}{4}$}, \\ \left( \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{array} \right) & \text{if $i=4$}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eqn:Jacobian_3M

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: If $(d_1,d_2)\in S$, we have $3d_2^2+(ud_1)^2\leq\max\{3,u^2\}\leq 3$ and $d_2^2+3(ud_1)^2\leq\max\{1,3u^2\}\leq 3$. Hence, we have $d'_1\geq 0$ and $d'_2\geq 0$. Let $x=\frac{1+d_1+d_2}{2}$ and $y=\frac{1+d_2-d_1}{2}$. Then, $(d_1,d_2)\in S$ implies $\frac{1}{2}\leq x \leq 1$ and $0\leq y\leq 1$. In addition, a simple calculation yields $ d_1'+d_2'=3\left(\frac{x+ry}{1+r}\right)^2-2\left(\frac{x+ry}{1+r}\right)^3 \leq 1, $ where $r=\frac{1-u}{1+u}$. Note that $0\leq\frac{x+ry}{1+r}\leq 1$ and the function $f:z\mapsto 3z^2-2z^3$ satisfies $f(z)\leq f(1)=1$ for all $0\leq z\leq 1$.

nodes.name: Change of variables
nodes.statement: Let $x=\frac{1+d_1+d_2}{2}$ and $y=\frac{1+d_2-d_1}{2}$. Then, $(d_1,d_2)\in S$ implies $\frac{1}{2}\leq x \leq 1$ and $0\leq y\leq 1$.

nodes.statement: In addition, a simple calculation yields $ d_1'+d_2'=3\left(\frac{x+ry}{1+r}\right)^2-2\left(\frac{x+ry}{1+r}\right)^3 \leq 1, $ where $r=\frac{1-u}{1+u}$. Note that $0\leq\frac{x+ry}{1+r}\leq 1$ and the function $f:z\mapsto 3z^2-2z^3$ satisfies $f(z)\leq f(1)=1$ for all $0\leq z\leq 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.4
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to check that the points $\mathbf{d}^*_2$ and $-\mathbf{d}^*_2$ are sink. Therefore, \cref{prop:sink_3M} immediately follows from \cref{prop:sinkpoint}.
nodes.statement_short: $\pm\mathbf{d}^*_2$ are sink points; apply the general sink-point proposition.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5
nodes.statement: Note that $J_4$ is the all-zero matrix and the same holds at $-\mathbf{d}^*_4$. Let $\epsilon>0$ be sufficiently small constant. If $A$ satisfies $|A|\leq \epsilon n$, apply \cref{prop:fastconsensus_Jacob}. If $A$ satisfies $|A|\geq (2-\epsilon)n$, apply \cref{prop:fastconsensus_Jacob} for $V\setminus A$.
nodes.statement_short: $J_4=0$; apply the zero-Jacobian fast-consensus proposition to $A$ or to $V\setminus A$.

nodes.name: Zero Jacobian
nodes.statement: Note that $J_4$ is the all-zero matrix and the same holds at $-\mathbf{d}^*_4$. Let $\epsilon>0$ be sufficiently small constant.

nodes.name: Small $A$
nodes.statement: If $A$ satisfies $|A|\leq \epsilon n$, apply \cref{prop:fastconsensus_Jacob}.

nodes.name: Large $A$
nodes.statement: If $A$ satisfies $|A|\geq (2-\epsilon)n$, apply \cref{prop:fastconsensus_Jacob} for $V\setminus A$.

nodes.name: Parameter regime
nodes.statement: Suppose that $u<\frac{3}{4}$ (or equivalently, $r>\frac{1}{7}$) and that $p\geq q\geq 0$ are constants.

nodes.name: Reduction and variance condition
nodes.statement: We prove that $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)=O(\log n)$ for any $A=A^{(0)}\subseteq V$. Consider the stochastic process $({\boldsymbol \delta}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$. From \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield,prop:fastconsensus_3M}, it suffices to show that $|\delta_2^{(\tau)}|>\epsilon_1$ holds w.h.p.~for some constant $\epsilon_1>0$ and some $\tau=O(\log n)$. To this end, we use \cref{prop:escape}. From \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield}, we may assume \begin{align} {\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)}\in \bigcup_{i\in\{1,2\}}B(\mathbf{d}^*_i,\epsilon_2) \end{align} for any constant $\epsilon_2>0$. We check the condition~\ref{asm:asm2} of Assumption~\ref{asm:escape_assumption0}. To this end, we show the following result: \begin{theorem}[Concentration of the variance for the Best-of-three] Consider the Best-of-three on $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$. Then, two constants $C_1,C_2>0$ exist such that \begin{align*} \forall A\subseteq V, \, \forall i\in\{1,2\}\,:\, \left|\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}\left[|A'_i|\,\middle|\, A \right] - n\cdot g\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right) \right| \leq C_2\sqrt{\frac{n}{p}}, \end{align*} where $g(x)\mathrel{\mathop:}= f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x)(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x))$. \end{theorem} \begin{proof} That variance $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A]$ can be represented as \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A] = \sum_{v\in V_i} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[v\in A'](1-\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[v\in A']) = \sum_{v\in V_i} f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) \left(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)\right). \end{align*} Therefore, \cref{thm:mainthm_Var} immediately follows from property~\ref{pro:gomiN}. \end{proof} From \cref{thm:mainthm_Var}, a straightforward calculation leads to \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha'_i \mid A] &= \frac{1}{n^2}\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A] \\ &= \frac{(3z_i^2-2z_i^3)\bigl(1-(3z_i^2-2z_i^3)\bigr)}{n} \pm O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^3p}}\right) \\ &=\frac{z_i^2(3-2z_i)(1-z_i)^2(2z_i+1)}{n} \pm O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^3p}}\right), \end{align*} where $z_i=\frac{a_i+ra_{3-i}}{1+r}$. If $|\delta_2|<1-\epsilon_3$ (or equivalently, $\epsilon_3<|a_1+a_2|<2-\epsilon_3$) for some constant $\epsilon_3>0$, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha'_i]=\Omega(n^{-1})$. Hence, the statement~\ref{asm:asm2} holds for every ${\boldsymbol \delta}$ satisfying ${\boldsymbol \delta} \in \bigcup_{i\in\{1,2\}}B(\mathbf{d}^*_i,\epsilon_2)$ with sufficiently small constant $\epsilon_2<1$ mentioned in \cref{eqn:initial_assumption}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to escaping in $\delta_2$ and verify (A2) via the variance concentration.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Consider the stochastic process $({\boldsymbol \delta}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$. From \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield,prop:fastconsensus_3M}, it suffices to show that $|\delta_2^{(\tau)}|>\epsilon_1$ holds w.h.p.~for some constant $\epsilon_1>0$ and some $\tau=O(\log n)$. To this end, we use \cref{prop:escape}.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to make $|\delta_2|$ exceed a constant in $O(\log n)$ steps.

nodes.name: Start near $\mathbf{d}^*_1$ or $\mathbf{d}^*_2$
nodes.statement: From \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield}, we may assume \begin{align} {\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)}\in \bigcup_{i\in\{1,2\}}B(\mathbf{d}^*_i,\epsilon_2) \end{align} for any constant $\epsilon_2>0$.

nodes.name: Initial position near $\mathbf{d}^*_1$ or $\mathbf{d}^*_2$
nodes.statement: {\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)}\in \bigcup_{i\in\{1,2\}}B(\mathbf{d}^*_i,\epsilon_2)
nodes.label: eqn:initial_assumption

nodes.name: Variance theorem
nodes.statement: We check the condition~\ref{asm:asm2} of Assumption~\ref{asm:escape_assumption0}. To this end, we show the following result: \begin{theorem}[Concentration of the variance for the Best-of-three] Consider the Best-of-three on $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$. Then, two constants $C_1,C_2>0$ exist such that \begin{align*} \forall A\subseteq V, \, \forall i\in\{1,2\}\,:\, \left|\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}\left[|A'_i|\,\middle|\, A \right] - n\cdot g\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right) \right| \leq C_2\sqrt{\frac{n}{p}}, \end{align*} where $g(x)\mathrel{\mathop:}= f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x)(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x))$. \end{theorem} \begin{proof} That variance $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A]$ can be represented as \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A] = \sum_{v\in V_i} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[v\in A'](1-\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[v\in A']) = \sum_{v\in V_i} f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) \left(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)\right). \end{align*} Therefore, \cref{thm:mainthm_Var} immediately follows from property~\ref{pro:gomiN}. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: State and prove the variance concentration theorem.

nodes.name: Concentration of the variance for the Best-of-three
nodes.statement: Consider the Best-of-three on $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$. Then, two constants $C_1,C_2>0$ exist such that \begin{align*} \forall A\subseteq V, \, \forall i\in\{1,2\}\,:\, \left|\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}\left[|A'_i|\,\middle|\, A \right] - n\cdot g\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right) \right| \leq C_2\sqrt{\frac{n}{p}}, \end{align*} where $g(x)\mathrel{\mathop:}= f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x)(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(x))$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{Var}[|A'_i|\mid A]$ equals $n\,g$ of the weighted density up to $O(\sqrt{n/p})$, with $g=f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.9
nodes.statement: That variance $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A]$ can be represented as \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A] = \sum_{v\in V_i} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[v\in A'](1-\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[v\in A']) = \sum_{v\in V_i} f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right) \left(1-f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)\right). \end{align*} Therefore, \cref{thm:mainthm_Var} immediately follows from property~\ref{pro:gomiN}.
nodes.statement_short: Write the variance as a sum of $g(\deg_A(v)/\deg(v))$ and apply (P2).

nodes.name: Variance estimate
nodes.statement: From \cref{thm:mainthm_Var}, a straightforward calculation leads to \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha'_i \mid A] &= \frac{1}{n^2}\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|A'_i| \mid A] \\ &= \frac{(3z_i^2-2z_i^3)\bigl(1-(3z_i^2-2z_i^3)\bigr)}{n} \pm O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^3p}}\right) \\ &=\frac{z_i^2(3-2z_i)(1-z_i)^2(2z_i+1)}{n} \pm O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^3p}}\right), \end{align*} where $z_i=\frac{a_i+ra_{3-i}}{1+r}$. If $|\delta_2|<1-\epsilon_3$ (or equivalently, $\epsilon_3<|a_1+a_2|<2-\epsilon_3$) for some constant $\epsilon_3>0$, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha'_i]=\Omega(n^{-1})$.

nodes.name: (A2) holds
nodes.statement: Hence, the statement~\ref{asm:asm2} holds for every ${\boldsymbol \delta}$ satisfying ${\boldsymbol \delta} \in \bigcup_{i\in\{1,2\}}B(\mathbf{d}^*_i,\epsilon_2)$ with sufficiently small constant $\epsilon_2<1$ mentioned in \cref{eqn:initial_assumption}.

nodes.name: Subcase $u<2/3$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $u<\frac{2}{3}$. Then the fixed point $\mathbf{d}^*_2$ does not exist and thus we assume ${\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)} \in B(\mathbf{d}^*_1,\epsilon_2)$. From \cref{prop:escape}, we have $|\delta_2^{(\tau)}|>\epsilon_2$ for some $\tau=O(\log n)$ (note that ${\boldsymbol \beta}=(\beta_1,\beta_2)$ of \cref{eqn:betadef} is given by ${\boldsymbol \beta}={\boldsymbol \delta}$ and the eigenvalues satisfy $0\leq \lambda_1 < 1 < \lambda_2$).

nodes.statement: Suppose that $u>\frac{2}{3}$. Both eigenvalues of $J_1$ are strictly larger than $1$. Hence, for $\mathbf{d}^*_1$, \cref{prop:escape} implies that either $|\delta_1^{(\tau)}|>\epsilon_2$ or $|\delta_2^{(\tau)}|>\epsilon_2$ holds for some $\tau=O(\log n)$ if ${\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)} \in B(\mathbf{d}^*_1,\epsilon_2)$. Note that, at the point $\mathbf{d}^*_2$, the Jacobian matrix $J_2$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ satisfying $0<\lambda_1<1<\lambda_2$. Moreover, in look at \cref{eqn:betadef}, we have ${\boldsymbol \beta}={\boldsymbol \delta}-\mathbf{d}^*_2$. nodes.name: Case $u=2/3$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{The case of $u=\frac{2}{3}$.} In this case, we have $\mathbf{d}^*_1=\mathbf{d}^*_2=(0,0)$. We claim that this point satisfies \ref{asm:asm4} and \ref{asm:asm5} and then apply \cref{prop:escape}. Let $\epsilon_2>0$ be sufficiently small constant mentioned in \cref{eqn:initial_assumption}. The Jacobian matrix $J_1=J_2$ has eigenvalues $1$ and $\frac{3}{2}$. Suppose that $\|{\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon_2$ for sufficiently small constant $\epsilon_2>0$. Then, we have \begin{align*} |\mathbf{E}[\delta_2' \mid A]|&=\left|\frac{\delta_2}{2}(3-3(u\delta_1)^2-\delta_2^2)\right| \pm O(n^{-0.5}) \\ & \geq |\delta_2|\left(\frac{3}{2} - O_{\epsilon_2\to 0}(\epsilon_2)\right) - O(n^{-0.5}) \\ &\geq 1.49 |\delta_2| - O(n^{-0.5}). \end{align*} This verifies the assumption~\ref{asm:asm4}. On the other hand, for any ${\boldsymbol \delta}$ of $|\delta_1|\leq\epsilon_2$, we have \begin{align} \left|\mathbf{E}[\delta_1' \mid A]\right|&=\left|\frac{u\delta_1}{2}\right|\left|3-(u\delta_1)^2-3\delta_2^2\right| \pm O(n^{-0.5}) \nonumber\\ &\leq |\delta_1|\left|1 - \frac{4}{27} \delta_1^2\right| + O(n^{-0.5}) \nonumber\\ &\leq |\delta_1|\left(1 - \frac{4}{27} \delta_1^2\right) + O(n^{-0.5}). \end{align} By applying the Hoeffding bound (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}) to the random variables $\delta_1=\alpha_1-\alpha_2$ and $\delta_2=\alpha_1+\alpha_2-\frac{1}{2}$, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|\delta'_i-\mathbf{E}[\delta'_i]|\geq t\right] \leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(nt^2\right)\right). \end{align*} In particular, letting $t=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$, we have \begin{align} \delta'_i=\mathbf{E}[\delta'_i] \pm O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right) \end{align} holds w.h.p. We claim that \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|\delta'_1|\leq\epsilon_2 \,\middle|\,|\delta_1|\leq\epsilon_2\right] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)} \end{align*} holds, which is equivalent to \ref{asm:asm5}. From \cref{eqn:gamma1_exp_bound,eqn:gamma_bound}, if $|\delta_1|\leq\epsilon_2$, we have \begin{align*} |\delta'_1| \leq |\delta_1| - \frac{4}{27}|\delta_1|^3 + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \end{align*} for sufficiently large constant $C>0$ and large $n$. If $|\delta_1|^3\geq \frac{27C}{4}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$, we have $|\delta'_1|\leq |\delta_1|\leq \epsilon_2$ holds w.h.p. If $|\delta_1|^3 < \frac{27C}{4}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$, we have $|\delta'_1|=O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)\leq \epsilon_2$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: At the merged fixed point verify (A4) and (A5) directly and apply the escape proposition.

nodes.name: Merged fixed point

Suppose that $\|{\boldsymbol \delta}^{(0)}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon_2$ for sufficiently small constant $\epsilon_2>0$. Then, we have \begin{align*} |\mathbf{E}[\delta_2' \mid A]|&=\left|\frac{\delta_2}{2}(3-3(u\delta_1)^2-\delta_2^2)\right| \pm O(n^{-0.5}) \\ & \geq |\delta_2|\left(\frac{3}{2} - O_{\epsilon_2\to 0}(\epsilon_2)\right) - O(n^{-0.5}) \\ &\geq 1.49 |\delta_2| - O(n^{-0.5}). \end{align*} This verifies the assumption~\ref{asm:asm4}.

nodes.statement: Thus, from \cref{prop:escape}, we have $|\delta^{(\tau)}_2|>\epsilon_2$ w.h.p.~for some $\tau=O(\log n)$. This completes the proof of \cref{thm:worst_case_3M}.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.3
nodes.statement: If $u=1$, we have \begin{align*} d'_1+d'_2 &= f(d_1+d_2), \\ d'_1-d'_2 &= f(d_1-d_2), \end{align*} where $f:z\mapsto \frac{1}{2}z(3-z^2)$. Since $f(z)>z$ for $z\in(0,1)$, we have $\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbf{d}^{(t)}\in\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)\}$. In addition, if $d_2^{(0)}>0$ then $d_2^{(t)}\to 1$ as $t\to\infty$. Suppose that $0\leq u<1$. We use basic results of \emph{competitive dynamics} (see \cref{sec:competitive_system}). We first claim that the map $T:S\to S$ is competitive and it satisfies the conditions \ref{cond:map_condition1} to \ref{cond:map_condition4} described in \cref{sec:competitive_system}. Then, we apply \cref{thm:orbit_convergence} and complete the proof of the first statement. To this end, we consider the Jacobian matrix $J$ given in \cref{eqn:general_Jacobian_3M}. The condition \ref{cond:map_condition1} follows from \cref{lem:criterion_C1}: it is straightforward to check that the Jacobian matrix \cref{eqn:general_Jacobian_3M} satisfies the condition of \cref{lem:criterion_C1}. To verify the condition \ref{cond:map_condition2}, we use the Inverse Function Theorem (\cref{thm:IFT}). We claim that $\det J>0$ for any $\mathbf{d}\in S\setminus\{(0,1)\}$. Indeed, in look at \cref{eqn:general_Jacobian_3M}, we have \begin{align} \det J = \frac{9u}{4}(1-(ud_1-d_2)^2)(1-(ud_1+d_2)^2) \geq \frac{9u}{4}(1-ud_1-d_2)^4 >0 \end{align} for $(d_1,d_2)\in S\setminus \{(0,1)\}$. Hence, for any $\mathbf{d}\in S\setminus \{(0,1)\}$, an inverse mapping $T^{-1}(\mathbf{d})$ is defined. Moreover, it is straightforward to check that $T(\mathbf{x})=(0,1)$ if and only if $\mathbf{x}=(0,1)$. Consequently, $T$ is injective. The condition \ref{cond:map_condition3} immediately follows from the definition \cref{eqn:3Mvecfielddef}. To condition \ref{cond:map_condition4} follows from \cref{lem:criterion_C4} and \cref{eqn:positive_det_3M}. Now we apply \cref{thm:orbit_convergence} and complete the proof of the first claim of \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield}. To obtain the second claim of \cref{prop:3Mvectorfield}, we show that $d'_2>0$ whenever $(d_1,d_2)\in S$ satisfies $d_2>0$ (here, $d_2>0$ means that $d_2>c$ for some constant $c>0$; we do not deal with the case of $d_2\geq o(1)$). This follows from a simple calculation \begin{align*} d'_2 \geq \frac{d_2}{2}(3-3d_1^2-d_2^2) \geq \frac{d_2}{2}(3-3d_1-d_2) \geq d_2^2 >0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For $u<1$ show $T$ is a competitive, injective $C^1$ map with monotone inverse (Jacobian sign pattern, $\det J>0$) and apply the competitive-map convergence theorem; $d_2$ stays positive for the second claim.

Since $f(z)>z$ for $z\in(0,1)$, we have $\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbf{d}^{(t)}\in\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)\}$. In addition, if $d_2^{(0)}>0$ then $d_2^{(t)}\to 1$ as $t\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Discrepancy of $W$ from its ideal value $\hat W$
nodes.statement: For a vertex set $V$ with $|V|=N$, let $(I_e)_{e\in \binom{V}{2}}$ be $\binom{N}{2}$ independent binary random variables. Let $p \mathrel{\mathop:}= \max_{e\in \binom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[I_e]$. Suppose that $N p \geq 1$. For $\ell+1$ vertex subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$, let \begin{align*} W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)&\mathrel{\mathop:}=\sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in[\ell]}\deg_{S_i}(s), \\ \hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in[\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)] \end{align*} where $\deg_S(v)=\sum_{s\in S\setminus \{v\}}I_{\{v,s\}}$ for $S\subseteq V$ and $v\in V$. Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-N^{-C_1}$: \begin{align*} \forall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: \bigl|W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)-\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)\bigr| \leq C_2N (N p)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For independent edge indicators with $Np\ge1$, uniformly over all vertex subsets $|W-\hat W|\le C_2N(Np)^{\ell-1/2}$ w.h.p., where $W$ sums products of degrees into sets.

nodes.name: Proof of (P2) of Theorem 3.2 via Lemma 8.1
nodes.statement: Let $f(x)=\sum_{j=0}^\ell c_jx^j$. For notational convenience, let $x_v=\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}$, $\bar{x}_v=\frac{\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]}{\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]}$ and $\hat{x}=\frac{|A_{i}|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}$. Then from the triangle inequality, it holds that \begin{align} \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right| &\leq \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\bar{x}_v)\bigr)\right|+\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right|. \end{align} For the second term of the right hand of \cref{eq:trianglegomi}, two positive constant $C_1, C_2$ exist such that \begin{align*} \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right| \leq \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}|f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})| \leq C_1\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}|\bar{x}_v-\hat{x}| \leq C_2\frac{|S\cap V_i|}{n} \leq C_2. \end{align*} The second inequality follows from the Lipschitz condition of $f$ (c.f.~\cref{sec:lipschitzcondition}). The third inequality holds since $\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]=(n-1)p+nq$ and $(|A_{i}|-1)p+|A_{3-i}|q \leq \mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]\leq |A_{i}|p+|A_{3-i}|q$ for any $v\in V_i$. For the first term of the right hand of \cref{eq:trianglegomi}, since \begin{align*} \left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)^j-\left(\frac{\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]}{\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]}\right)^j &=\frac{\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^j-\deg(v)^j\right)\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)^j+\left(\deg_A(v)^j-\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]^j\right)}{\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^j} \end{align*} for any $j$ and $v\in V$, we have \begin{align*} \lefteqn{\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\bar{x}_v)\bigr)\right| =\left|\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}c_j \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left((x_v)^j-(\bar{x}_v)^j\right)\right|}\\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^\ell \frac{|c_j|}{((n-1)p)^j} \left(\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^{j}-\deg(v)^j\right)\left(x_v\right)^j \right|+\left| \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\deg_A(v)^j-\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]^j\right)\right|\right). \end{align*} Note that $\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]=(n-1)p+nq\geq (n-1)p$ for any $v\in V$. Since \begin{align*} \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^{j}-\deg(v)^j\right)\left(x_v\right)^j \right| &\leq \max_{U\subseteq V}\left|\sum_{u\in U}\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(u)]^{j}-\deg(u)^j\right)\right|\\ &=\max_{U\subseteq V}\left|W(U;\overbrace{V,\ldots,V}^{j})-\hat{W}(U;\overbrace{V,\ldots,V}^{j})\right| \end{align*} and $\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\deg_A(v)^j-\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]^j\right)=W(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j})-\hat{W}(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j})$, we obtain the claim from \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy}. Note that, for any $S\subseteq V$, $a\in \mathbb{R}^V$ and $x\in [0,1]^V$, $|\sum_{s\in S}a_sx_s|\leq \max_{U\subseteq V}|\sum_{u\in U}a_u|$ since $\sum_{s\in S:a_s\leq 0}a_s \leq \sum_{s\in S}a_sx_s\leq \sum_{s\in S:a_s\geq 0}a_s$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality splits the error; the ideal-vs-mean term is bounded by Lipschitz continuity and the random term is rewritten as $W-\hat W$ discrepancies bounded by Lemma 8.1.

nodes.name: Notation and split
nodes.statement: Let $f(x)=\sum_{j=0}^\ell c_jx^j$. For notational convenience, let $x_v=\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}$, $\bar{x}_v=\frac{\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]}{\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]}$ and $\hat{x}=\frac{|A_{i}|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}$. Then from the triangle inequality, it holds that \begin{align} \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right| &\leq \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\bar{x}_v)\bigr)\right|+\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $x_v,\bar x_v,\hat x$ and split by the triangle inequality (16).

nodes.name: Triangle-inequality split
nodes.statement: \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right| &\leq \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\bar{x}_v)\bigr)\right|+\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right|.
nodes.label: eq:trianglegomi

nodes.name: Deterministic term
nodes.statement: For the second term of the right hand of \cref{eq:trianglegomi}, two positive constant $C_1, C_2$ exist such that \begin{align*} \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})\bigr)\right| \leq \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}|f(\bar{x}_v)-f(\hat{x})| \leq C_1\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}|\bar{x}_v-\hat{x}| \leq C_2\frac{|S\cap V_i|}{n} \leq C_2. \end{align*} The second inequality follows from the Lipschitz condition of $f$ (c.f.~\cref{sec:lipschitzcondition}). The third inequality holds since $\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]=(n-1)p+nq$ and $(|A_{i}|-1)p+|A_{3-i}|q \leq \mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]\leq |A_{i}|p+|A_{3-i}|q$ for any $v\in V_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz continuity bounds the mean-vs-ideal term by a constant.

nodes.name: Random term expansion
nodes.statement: For the first term of the right hand of \cref{eq:trianglegomi}, since \begin{align*} \left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)^j-\left(\frac{\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]}{\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]}\right)^j &=\frac{\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^j-\deg(v)^j\right)\left(\frac{\deg_A(v)}{\deg(v)}\right)^j+\left(\deg_A(v)^j-\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]^j\right)}{\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^j} \end{align*} for any $j$ and $v\in V$, we have \begin{align*} \lefteqn{\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\bigl(f(x_v)-f(\bar{x}_v)\bigr)\right| =\left|\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}c_j \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left((x_v)^j-(\bar{x}_v)^j\right)\right|}\\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^\ell \frac{|c_j|}{((n-1)p)^j} \left(\left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^{j}-\deg(v)^j\right)\left(x_v\right)^j \right|+\left| \sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\deg_A(v)^j-\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]^j\right)\right|\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand monomial differences of degree ratios.

nodes.name: Reduce to $W$
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]=(n-1)p+nq\geq (n-1)p$ for any $v\in V$. Since \begin{align*} \left|\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]^{j}-\deg(v)^j\right)\left(x_v\right)^j \right| &\leq \max_{U\subseteq V}\left|\sum_{u\in U}\left(\mathbf{E}[\deg(u)]^{j}-\deg(u)^j\right)\right|\\ &=\max_{U\subseteq V}\left|W(U;\overbrace{V,\ldots,V}^{j})-\hat{W}(U;\overbrace{V,\ldots,V}^{j})\right| \end{align*} and $\sum_{v\in S\cap V_i}\left(\deg_A(v)^j-\mathbf{E}[\deg_A(v)]^j\right)=W(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j})-\hat{W}(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j})$, we obtain the claim from \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy}. Note that, for any $S\subseteq V$, $a\in \mathbb{R}^V$ and $x\in [0,1]^V$, $|\sum_{s\in S}a_sx_s|\leq \max_{U\subseteq V}|\sum_{u\in U}a_u|$ since $\sum_{s\in S:a_s\leq 0}a_s \leq \sum_{s\in S}a_sx_s\leq \sum_{s\in S:a_s\geq 0}a_s$.
nodes.statement_short: Express the sums as $W-\hat W$ and apply Lemma 8.1.

nodes.name: Key counting lemma (Bell-number bound)
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a set of $|V|=N$ vertices and fix $l+1$ subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_l\subseteq V$. For any $\mathbf{s}=(s_0,s_1,\ldots, s_l)\in S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l$, define \begin{align*} U(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \{s_i: i\in \{0\}\cup [l]\}. \end{align*} Consider $\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|}$, where $p\in [1/N,1]$, $\mathcal{S}\subseteq S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l$ and \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}: S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l \to 2^{\binom{V}{2}}. \end{align*} Suppose that the following three conditions hold for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}$: (1) $|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|\leq k$, (2) $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\subseteq \binom{U(\mathbf{s})}{2}$ and (3) the graph $G(\mathbf{s})=\bigl(U(\mathbf{s}), \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\bigr)$ is connected. Let $L\subseteq \{0\}\cup [l]$ be the set of indices such that $S_i\cap S_j=\emptyset$ for any $i,j\in L$ $(i\neq j)$. Then \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|}\leq \mathcal{B}_{l+1}N (N p)^k\frac{\prod_{i\in L}|S_i|}{N ^{|L|}} \end{align*} where $\mathcal{B}_l$ denotes the $l$-th Bell number.
nodes.statement_short: Sums of $p^{|\mathcal F(\mathbf s)|}$ over tuples whose edge sets form connected graphs with at most $k$ edges are at most $\mathcal B_{l+1}N(Np)^k\prod_{i\in L}|S_i|/N^{|L|}$.
nodes.label: lem:technique

nodes.name: Bell number
nodes.statement: The $l$-th {\em Bell number} $\mathcal{B}_l$ is the number of possible partitions of a set with $l$ labeled elements.

nodes.name: Upper bound on Bell numbers (Berend-Tassa)
nodes.statement: It is known that $\mathcal{B}_{l}<\left(\frac{0.792 l}{\ln(l+1)}\right)^l$ for all positive integer $l$ \cite{DT10}.
conclusions: $\mathcal{B}_{l}<\left(\frac{0.792 l}{\ln(l+1)}\right)^l$

nodes.name: Concentration of $W$
nodes.statement: Suppose the same setting of \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy}. Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-N^{-C_1}$: \begin{align*} \forall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: \bigl|W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)-\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]\bigr|\leq C_2 N(N p)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Uniformly over all vertex subsets, $|W-\mathbf{E}W|\le C_2N(Np)^{\ell-1/2}$ with probability $1-N^{-C_1}$.
conclusions: Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-N^{-C_1}$:
nodes.label: lem:WEWdiscrepancy
