eq j$ and $\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|=\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|\{a_{i-(\ell+1)}\}|=1$) yields  egin{align} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|-|A|} = rac{1}{p^{\kappa}}\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} \leq  rac{1}{p^{\kappa}} \mathcal{B}_{\ell+\kappa+2} N(Np)^{\ell} rac{\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|}{N^{\kappa+1}} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-\kappa}. \end{align} Combining \cref{eq:YAzero,eq:YApositive}, we have  egin{align*} \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{ 2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(Np)^{\ell-|A|}=\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-1}, \ \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &=\max\left\{ \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}], \mathbf{E}[d_\ell(V)] ight\} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N(Np)^{\ell}. \end{align*} Thus from \cref{eq:KimVutoY} with $\lambda=(2(\ell-1)+C_7/2)\log N$ and $C_8=\sqrt{\ell!} \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)} (16(\ell-1+C_7/2))^\ell$, we obtain  egin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq C_8\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}ight]\leq 2\mathrm{e}^2/N^{C_7}. \end{align} Combining \cref{eq:WdlV}, \cref{claim:WEWlower} and \cref{claim:dlV}, the following holds with probability at least $1-2e^2/N^{C_7}-1/N^{C_3}$:  egin{align*} & orall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: \ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell}) \leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell})]+C_9\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}+(\ell+1)C_4 N (Np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align*} Thus we obtain the claim \cref{claim:WEWupper} and combining the claims \cref{claim:WEWlower,claim:WEWupper} complete the proof of \cref{lem:WEWdiscrepancy}.
nodes.statement_short: Lower tail: Janson's inequality with a union bound over all subsets, bounding $\nabla$ by the counting lemma. Upper tail: write $W$ as $W(V;V,\dots,V)$ minus lower-bounded terms and control $W(V;\dots)$ by Kim-Vu.

nodes.name: Edge-set representation
nodes.statement: For $\ell+1$ vertex subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$, let \begin{align*} \mathbf{S}&\mathrel{\mathop:}=\left\{(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_\ell): s_0\in S_0, s_i \in S_i\setminus \{s_0\}\ \textrm{for every $i\in [\ell]$}\right\} \end{align*} and for any $\mathbf{s}=(s_0, s_1,\ldots, s_\ell)\in \prod_{i=0}^\ell S_i=S_0 \times S_1\times \cdots \times S_\ell$, let \begin{align*} F(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \bigl\{\{s_0,s_i\}: i\in [\ell] \bigr\}\setminus \{s_0\}. \end{align*} For example, $F\bigl((a,b,a,c,d,b,f,a)\bigr)=\bigl\{\{a,b\},\{a,c\},\{a,d\},\{a,f\}\bigr\}$. Then, \begin{align} W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell) &=\sum_{s_0\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\left(\sum_{s_i\in S_i\setminus \{s_0\}}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right) =\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}\prod_{i\in [\ell]} I_{\{s_0,s_i\}} =\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})} I_{e}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write $W$ as a sum over tuples of products of edge indicators (17).

nodes.name: $W$ as a polynomial in edge indicators
nodes.statement: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell) &=\sum_{s_0\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\left(\sum_{s_i\in S_i\setminus \{s_0\}}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right) =\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}\prod_{i\in [\ell]} I_{\{s_0,s_i\}} =\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})} I_{e}.
nodes.label: eq:WtoJ

nodes.name: Lower bound on $W$
nodes.statement_short: Janson's inequality plus the counting lemma give the uniform lower bound (18).

nodes.name: Claim (18)
nodes.statement: First, we claim the following: Two positive constants $C_3, C_4$ exist such that \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\forall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\geq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]-C_4 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} \right]\geq 1-N^{-C_3}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Uniform lower bound on $W$
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\forall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\geq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]-C_4 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} \right]\geq 1-N^{-C_3}.
conclusions: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\forall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\geq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]-C_4 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} \right]\geq 1-N^{-C_3}.
nodes.label: claim:WEWlower

nodes.name: Janson + union bound
Janson bound with union bound
nodes.statement:
\lefteqn{\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\exists S_0,S_1,\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]-tight]} 
onumber \ &\leq \left(2^Night)^{\ell+1}\exp\left(- rac{t^2}{2
abla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)}ight) \leq \exp\left((\ell+1)N- rac{t^2}{2
abla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)}ight)
nodes.label: eq:WJansonwithNabla

nodes.name: Reduction to $\nabla$
nodes.statement: Thus it suffices to show that $ \nabla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell) = O(N (N p)^{2\ell-1}) $.

nodes.name: Bound $\nabla$ by $p$-powers
nodes.statement:
Since $\max_{e\in  inom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[J_e]=p$, it holds that  egin{align} 
abla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell) &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S},\mathbf{s}'\in \mathbf{S}:\F(\mathbf{s})\cap F(\mathbf{s}')
eq \emptyset}} \mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})} I_{e}\prod_{e'\in F(\mathbf{s}')} I_{e'}ight] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S},\mathbf{s}'\in \mathbf{S}:\F(\mathbf{s})\cap F(\mathbf{s}')
eq \emptyset}} p^{|F(\mathbf{s})\cup F(\mathbf{s}')|}. \end{align} To bound \cref{eq:nablaupper1}, we apply \cref{lem:technique} which we will prove in \cref{sec:technique}.

nodes.name: First bound on $\nabla$
nodes.statement:
abla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell) &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S},\mathbf{s}'\in \mathbf{S}:\F(\mathbf{s})\cap F(\mathbf{s}')
eq \emptyset}} \mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})} I_{e}\prod_{e'\in F(\mathbf{s}')} I_{e'}ight] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S},\mathbf{s}'\in \mathbf{S}:\F(\mathbf{s})\cap F(\mathbf{s}')
eq \emptyset}} p^{|F(\mathbf{s})\cup F(\mathbf{s}')|}.
nodes.label: eq:nablaupper1

nodes.name: Apply counting lemma
nodes.statement: Consider $2\ell+2$ vertex subsets $S'_0, S'_1, \ldots, S'_{2\ell+1}$ where $S'_i\mathrel{\mathop:}= S_{i\bmod (\ell+1)}$. For any $i\in \{0\}\cup [2\ell+1]$, let \begin{align*} \mathcal{S}&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \left\{ (s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{2\ell+1})\in \mathbf{S}\times \mathbf{S} : F\bigl((s_0, \ldots, s_{\ell})\bigr)\cap F\bigl((s_{\ell+1},\ldots, s_{2\ell+1})\bigr)\neq \emptyset \right\}\subseteq \prod_{i=0}^{2\ell+1}S'_i, \\ \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= F\bigl((s_0, \ldots, s_{\ell})\bigr)\cup F\bigl((s_{\ell+1},\ldots, s_{2\ell+1})\bigr)\ \textrm{for any}\ \mathbf{s}=(s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{2\ell+1})\in \prod_{i=0}^{2\ell+1}S'_i. \end{align*} Then for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}$, $G({\mathbf{s}})=\bigl(U({\mathbf{s}}), \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\bigr)$ is a connected graph and $|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|\leq 2\ell-1$. Thus, for any $i_* \in \{0\} \cup [\ell]$, \cref{lem:technique} with letting $l=2\ell+1,k=2\ell-1$ and $L=\{i_*\}$ yields \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S},\mathbf{s}'\in \mathbf{S}:\\F(\mathbf{s})\cap F(\mathbf{s}')\neq \emptyset}} p^{|F(\mathbf{s})\cup F(\mathbf{s}')|} &=\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N(Np)^{2\ell-1}\frac{|S_{i_*}'|}{N} =\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{2\ell-1}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Second bound on $\nabla$
nodes.statement: \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S},\mathbf{s}'\in \mathbf{S}:\\F(\mathbf{s})\cap F(\mathbf{s}')\neq \emptyset}} p^{|F(\mathbf{s})\cup F(\mathbf{s}')|} &=\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N(Np)^{2\ell-1}\frac{|S_{i_*}'|}{N} =\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{2\ell-1}.
nodes.label: eq:nablaupper2

nodes.name: Claim (22)
nodes.statement: Equations~\cref{eq:nablaupper1,eq:nablaupper2} imply the following statement: For any $\ell+1$ vertex subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots S_\ell$ and for any $i_*\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$, \begin{align} \nabla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell) &\leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{2\ell-1} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N (N p)^{2\ell-1}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Bound on $\nabla$
nodes.statement: \nabla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell) &\leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{2\ell-1} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N (N p)^{2\ell-1}.
conclusions: \nabla(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell) &\leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{2\ell-1} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N (N p)^{2\ell-1}.
nodes.label: claim:nablaupper

nodes.name: Conclude (18)
nodes.statement: Thus by substituting $t=C_4 N(N p)^{\ell-1/2}$ with $C_4=\sqrt{2(\ell+1+C_3)\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}}$ to \cref{eq:WJansonwithNabla}, we obtain the claim \cref{claim:WEWlower}.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $W$
nodes.statement:
extbf{Upper bound on $W$. } To complete the proof of \cref{lem:WEWdiscrepancy}, we combine the claim \cref{claim:WEWlower} and the following claim: Two positive constants $C_5, C_6$ exist such that  egin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[ orall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]+C_6 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} ight]\geq 1-N^{-C_5}. \end{align} To show the claim, we consider the following expression of $W$. For any $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$, let $W_0\mathrel{\mathop:}= W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)$ and let $W_i\mathrel{\mathop:}= W(\overbrace{V; V\ldots, V}^{i}, S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell})$ for each $i\in[\ell+1]$. Since $W_{i+1}-W_{i}=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell})$ for any $i\in \{0\}\cup [\ell+1]$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{\ell}(W_{i+1}-W_{i})=W_{\ell+1}-W_0$, we have  egin{align} W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell})&=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})-\sum_{i=0}^{\ell}W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell}). \end{align} We can apply \cref{claim:WEWlower} for the second term of the right hand of \cref{eq:WdlV}. Now we try to get an upper bound on $W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})$. For the notational convenience, let $Y=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})$. Let $S_i=V$ for every $i\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$ and let  egin{align*} \mathcal{E}&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \left\{F(\mathbf{s}): \mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}ight\}. \end{align*} From \eqref{eq:WtoJ}, we have  egin{align*} Y =\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})}I_e =\sum_{F\in \mathcal{E}} |\{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S} : F(\mathbf{s})=F\}|\prod_{e\in F}I_e. \end{align*} Thus applying Kim-Vu inequality (\cref{lem:Kim-Vu}) to $Y$ yields  egin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq \sqrt{\ell! \max_{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]\max_{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}:A
eq \emptyset}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]}(8\lambda)^\ellight]\leq 2\exp(2+2(\ell-1)\log N-\lambda) \end{align} where  egin{align*} Y_{A} &=\sum_{\substack{F\in \mathcal{E}:\F\supseteq A}} |\{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}: F(\mathbf{s})=F\}|\prod_{e\in F\setminus A}I_e =\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})\setminus A}I_e. \end{align*} Now, we give an upper bound on $\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]$. Since $\max_{e\in  inom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[J_e]=p$, it holds that  egin{align*} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})\setminus A}I_eight] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})\setminus A|} =\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|-|A|}. \end{align*} If $A=\emptyset$, a direct application of \cref{lem:technique} with letting $l=k=\ell$ and $L=\emptyset$ yields  egin{align} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]=\mathbf{E}[Y] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}N (N p)^{\ell}. \end{align} Note that $|F(\mathbf{s})|\leq \ell$ and $G({\mathbf{s}})=(U(\mathbf{s}),F(\mathbf{s}))$ is a connected graph for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}\subseteq \prod_{i=0}^\ell S_i$. Now we consider the case $|A|=\kappa\geq 1$. Let $V(A)$ be the set of vertices induced by the edge set $A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}$. If $F(\mathbf{s})\supseteq A$ for some $\mathbf{s}\in \prod_{i=0}^\ell V$, the graph $G'=(V(A),A)$ is a star graph and hence $|V(A)|=|A|+1=\kappa+1$. Let $V(A)=\{a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{\kappa}\}$. Now consider $(\ell+1)+(\kappa+1)$ vertex subsets $S'_0, S'_1, \ldots S'_{\ell+\kappa+1}$ where $S'_i=S_i$ for any $0\leq i\leq \ell$ and $S'_i=\{a_{i-(\ell+1)}\}$ for any $\ell+1\leq i\leq \ell+\kappa+1$. Let  egin{align*} \mathcal{S}&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \left\{ (s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{\ell+\kappa+1})\in \mathbf{S}	imes \prod_{i=0}^{\kappa}\{a_i\}: F igl( (s_0,\ldots,s_\ell) igr)\supseteq A ight\}\subseteq \prod_{i=0}^{\ell+\kappa+1}S'_i,\ \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= F igl((s_0,\ldots,s_\ell) igr) \ 	extrm{for any}\ \mathbf{s}=(s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{\ell+\kappa+1})\in \prod_{i=0}^{\ell+\kappa+1}S'_i. \end{align*} Note that, for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}$, the graph $G({\mathbf{s}})= igl(U({\mathbf{s}}), \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s}) igr)$ is connected and $|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|\leq \ell$. Thus \cref{lem:technique} with letting $l=\ell+\kappa+1$, $k=\ell$ and $L=\{\ell+1, \ell+2, \ldots, \ell+\kappa+1\}$ (note that $a_i
eq a_j$ for any $i
eq j$ and $\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|=\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|\{a_{i-(\ell+1)}\}|=1$) yields  egin{align} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|-|A|} = rac{1}{p^{\kappa}}\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} \leq  rac{1}{p^{\kappa}} \mathcal{B}_{\ell+\kappa+2} N(Np)^{\ell} rac{\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|}{N^{\kappa+1}} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-\kappa}. \end{align} Combining \cref{eq:YAzero,eq:YApositive}, we have  egin{align*} \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{ 2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(Np)^{\ell-|A|}=\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-1}, \ \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &=\max\left\{ \max_{\substack{A\subseteq  inom{V}{2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}], \mathbf{E}[d_\ell(V)] ight\} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N(Np)^{\ell}. \end{align*} Thus from \cref{eq:KimVutoY} with $\lambda=(2(\ell-1)+C_7/2)\log N$ and $C_8=\sqrt{\ell!} \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)} (16(\ell-1+C_7/2))^\ell$, we obtain  egin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq C_8\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}ight]\leq 2\mathrm{e}^2/N^{C_7}. \end{align} Combining \cref{eq:WdlV}, \cref{claim:WEWlower} and \cref{claim:dlV}, the following holds with probability at least $1-2e^2/N^{C_7}-1/N^{C_3}$:  egin{align*} & orall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: \ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell}) \leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell})]+C_9\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}+(\ell+1)C_4 N (Np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align*} Thus we obtain the claim \cref{claim:WEWupper} and combining the claims \cref{claim:WEWlower,claim:WEWupper} complete the proof of \cref{lem:WEWdiscrepancy}.
nodes.statement_short: Telescoping reduces to $W(V;V,\dots,V)$, controlled by Kim-Vu.

nodes.name: Claim (23)
nodes.statement: To complete the proof of \cref{lem:WEWdiscrepancy}, we combine the claim \cref{claim:WEWlower} and the following claim: Two positive constants $C_5, C_6$ exist such that \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\forall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]+C_6 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} \right]\geq 1-N^{-C_5}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Uniform upper bound on $W$
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\forall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]+C_6 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} \right]\geq 1-N^{-C_5}.
conclusions: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\forall S_0, S_1\ldots, S_\ell: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots, S_\ell)]+C_6 N (N p)^{\ell-1/2} \right]\geq 1-N^{-C_5}.
nodes.label: claim:WEWupper

nodes.name: Telescoping
nodes.statement: To show the claim, we consider the following expression of $W$. For any $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$, let $W_0\mathrel{\mathop:}= W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)$ and let $W_i\mathrel{\mathop:}= W(\overbrace{V; V\ldots, V}^{i}, S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell})$ for each $i\in[\ell+1]$. Since $W_{i+1}-W_{i}=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell})$ for any $i\in \{0\}\cup [\ell+1]$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{\ell}(W_{i+1}-W_{i})=W_{\ell+1}-W_0$, we have \begin{align} W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell})&=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})-\sum_{i=0}^{\ell}W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell}). \end{align} We can apply \cref{claim:WEWlower} for the second term of the right hand of \cref{eq:WdlV}.

nodes.name: Telescoping identity for $W$
nodes.statement: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell})&=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})-\sum_{i=0}^{\ell}W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell}).
nodes.label: eq:WdlV

nodes.name: Define $Y$
nodes.statement: Now we try to get an upper bound on $W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})$. For the notational convenience, let $Y=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell+1})$.

nodes.name: Kim-Vu
nodes.statement: Let $S_i=V$ for every $i\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$ and let \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \left\{F(\mathbf{s}): \mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}\right\}. \end{align*} From \eqref{eq:WtoJ}, we have \begin{align*} Y =\sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})}I_e =\sum_{F\in \mathcal{E}} |\{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S} : F(\mathbf{s})=F\}|\prod_{e\in F}I_e. \end{align*} Thus applying Kim-Vu inequality (\cref{lem:Kim-Vu}) to $Y$ yields \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq \sqrt{\ell! \max_{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]\max_{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}:A\neq \emptyset}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]}(8\lambda)^\ell\right]\leq 2\exp(2+2(\ell-1)\log N-\lambda) \end{align} where \begin{align*} Y_{A} &=\sum_{\substack{F\in \mathcal{E}:\\F\supseteq A}} |\{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}: F(\mathbf{s})=F\}|\prod_{e\in F\setminus A}I_e =\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})\setminus A}I_e. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Kim-Vu bound for $Y$
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq \sqrt{\ell! \max_{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]\max_{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}:A\neq \emptyset}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]}(8\lambda)^\ell\right]\leq 2\exp(2+2(\ell-1)\log N-\lambda)
nodes.label: eq:KimVutoY

nodes.name: $\mathbf{E}[Y_\emptyset]$
nodes.statement: Now, we give an upper bound on $\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]$. Since $\max_{e\in \binom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[J_e]=p$, it holds that \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})\setminus A}I_e\right] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})\setminus A|} =\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|-|A|}. \end{align*} If $A=\emptyset$, a direct application of \cref{lem:technique} with letting $l=k=\ell$ and $L=\emptyset$ yields \begin{align} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]=\mathbf{E}[Y] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}N (N p)^{\ell}. \end{align} Note that $|F(\mathbf{s})|\leq \ell$ and $G({\mathbf{s}})=(U(\mathbf{s}),F(\mathbf{s}))$ is a connected graph for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}\subseteq \prod_{i=0}^\ell S_i$.

nodes.name: Bound on $\mathbf{E}[Y_A]$ for $A=\emptyset$
nodes.statement: \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}]=\mathbf{E}[Y] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}N (N p)^{\ell}.
nodes.label: eq:YAzero

nodes.name: $\mathbf{E}[Y_A]$, $|A|\ge1$
nodes.statement: Now we consider the case $|A|=\kappa\geq 1$. Let $V(A)$ be the set of vertices induced by the edge set $A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}$. If $F(\mathbf{s})\supseteq A$ for some $\mathbf{s}\in \prod_{i=0}^\ell V$, the graph $G'=(V(A),A)$ is a star graph and hence $|V(A)|=|A|+1=\kappa+1$. Let $V(A)=\{a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{\kappa}\}$. Now consider $(\ell+1)+(\kappa+1)$ vertex subsets $S'_0, S'_1, \ldots S'_{\ell+\kappa+1}$ where $S'_i=S_i$ for any $0\leq i\leq \ell$ and $S'_i=\{a_{i-(\ell+1)}\}$ for any $\ell+1\leq i\leq \ell+\kappa+1$. Let \begin{align*} \mathcal{S}&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \left\{ (s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{\ell+\kappa+1})\in \mathbf{S}\times \prod_{i=0}^{\kappa}\{a_i\}: F\bigl( (s_0,\ldots,s_\ell)\bigr)\supseteq A \right\}\subseteq \prod_{i=0}^{\ell+\kappa+1}S'_i,\\ \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= F\bigl((s_0,\ldots,s_\ell)\bigr) \ \textrm{for any}\ \mathbf{s}=(s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{\ell+\kappa+1})\in \prod_{i=0}^{\ell+\kappa+1}S'_i. \end{align*} Note that, for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}$, the graph $G({\mathbf{s}})=\bigl(U({\mathbf{s}}), \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\bigr)$ is connected and $|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|\leq \ell$. Thus \cref{lem:technique} with letting $l=\ell+\kappa+1$, $k=\ell$ and $L=\{\ell+1, \ell+2, \ldots, \ell+\kappa+1\}$ (note that $a_i\neq a_j$ for any $i\neq j$ and $\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|=\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|\{a_{i-(\ell+1)}\}|=1$) yields \begin{align} \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|-|A|} =\frac{1}{p^{\kappa}}\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \frac{1}{p^{\kappa}} \mathcal{B}_{\ell+\kappa+2} N(Np)^{\ell}\frac{\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|}{N^{\kappa+1}} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-\kappa}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Star structure plus counting lemma give (27).

nodes.name: Bound on $\mathbf{E}[Y_A]$ for $|A|\ge1$
nodes.statement: \mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ F(\mathbf{s}) \supseteq A}}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|-|A|} =\frac{1}{p^{\kappa}}\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \frac{1}{p^{\kappa}} \mathcal{B}_{\ell+\kappa+2} N(Np)^{\ell}\frac{\prod_{i=\ell+1}^{\ell+\kappa+1}|S'_i|}{N^{\kappa+1}} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-\kappa}.
nodes.label: eq:YApositive

nodes.name: Concentration of $Y$
nodes.statement: Combining \cref{eq:YAzero,eq:YApositive}, we have \begin{align*} \max_{\substack{A\subseteq \binom{V}{ 2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &\leq \max_{\substack{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(Np)^{\ell-|A|}=\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}(N p)^{\ell-1}, \\ \max_{\substack{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}] &=\max\left\{ \max_{\substack{A\subseteq \binom{V}{2}:|A|\geq 1}}\mathbf{E}[Y_{A}], \mathbf{E}[d_\ell(V)] \right\} \leq \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}N(Np)^{\ell}. \end{align*} Thus from \cref{eq:KimVutoY} with $\lambda=(2(\ell-1)+C_7/2)\log N$ and $C_8=\sqrt{\ell!} \mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)} (16(\ell-1+C_7/2))^\ell$, we obtain \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq C_8\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}\right]\leq 2\mathrm{e}^2/N^{C_7}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Concentration of $Y=W(V;V,\dots,V)$
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|Y-\mathbf{E}[Y]|\geq C_8\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}\right]\leq 2\mathrm{e}^2/N^{C_7}.
nodes.label: claim:dlV

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Combining \cref{eq:WdlV}, \cref{claim:WEWlower} and \cref{claim:dlV}, the following holds with probability at least $1-2e^2/N^{C_7}-1/N^{C_3}$: \begin{align*} &\forall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: \\ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell}) \leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell})]+C_9\sqrt{N }(\log N)^\ell (N p)^{\ell-1/2}+(\ell+1)C_4 N (Np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align*} Thus we obtain the claim \cref{claim:WEWupper} and combining the claims \cref{claim:WEWlower,claim:WEWupper} complete the proof of \cref{lem:WEWdiscrepancy}.

nodes.name: Discrepancy between $\mathbf{E}[W]$ and $\hat W$
nodes.statement: Suppose the same setting of \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy}. Then for any vertex subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$ and for any $i_*\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$, a positive constant $C$ exists such that \begin{align*} \left|\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]-\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)\right| \leq C|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{\ell-1}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 8.3 Discrepancy between the expected value and the ideal value
conclusions: a positive constant $C$ exists such that
nodes.label: lem:EWIdiscrepancy

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.4
nodes.statement: We show \begin{align*} \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)] \leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)] \leq \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)]+ \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}|S_{i_*}|(Np)^{\ell-1} \end{align*} for any $i_*\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$. The first inequality follows directly from the FKG inequality (\cref{lem:FKG}) since $\deg_{S_i}(s)$ is a monotone increase function on $(I_e)_{e\in \binom{V}{2}}$ for every $i$. Now we show the second inequality. We write each element $\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}$ as $\mathbf{s}=(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_\ell)$. Since $\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)] &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]. \end{align*} For the first term, since $s_i\neq s_j$ for any $i,j\in[\ell]$ ($i\neq j$) if $|F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell$, we obtain \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right] &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}\left[I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}\left[I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right] = \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)]. \end{align*} For the second term, from \cref{lem:technique}, \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})}I_{e}\right] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}|S_{i_*}|(Np)^{\ell-1}. \end{align*} Note that $G(\mathbf{s})=(U(\mathbf{s}),F(\mathbf{s}))$ is a connected graph for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by FKG; upper bound by splitting tuples into distinct-endpoint ones (product of means) and degenerate ones bounded by the counting lemma.

nodes.name: Two-sided bound
nodes.statement: We show \begin{align*} \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)] \leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)] \leq \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)]+ \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}|S_{i_*}|(Np)^{\ell-1} \end{align*} for any $i_*\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: Now we show the second inequality. We write each element $\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}$ as $\mathbf{s}=(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_\ell)$. Since $\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)] &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]. \end{align*} For the first term, since $s_i\neq s_j$ for any $i,j\in[\ell]$ ($i\neq j$) if $|F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell$, we obtain \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right] &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}\left[I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}\left[I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right] = \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in [\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)]. \end{align*} For the second term, from \cref{lem:technique}, \begin{align*} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{e\in F(\mathbf{s})}I_{e}\right] \leq \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}p^{|F(\mathbf{s})|} \leq \mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}|S_{i_*}|(Np)^{\ell-1}. \end{align*} Note that $G(\mathbf{s})=(U(\mathbf{s}),F(\mathbf{s}))$ is a connected graph for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}$.

Since $\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}}}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]$, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)] &=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|=\ell }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]+ \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathbf{S}:\\ |F(\mathbf{s})|\leq\ell-1 }}\mathbf{E}\left[\prod_{i\in [\ell]}I_{\{s_0,s_i\}}\right]. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Connectivity bound
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that \begin{align*} \forall \mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}: |U(\mathbf{s})|-1\leq |\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|\leq k \end{align*} since $G(\mathbf{s})=\bigl(U(\mathbf{s}),\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\bigr)$ is a connected graph from the assumption. nodes.label: eqn:C2_1

nodes.name: Partitions $R(\mathbf s)$
nodes.statement: To estimate above, we introduce the following notations. For any $(l+1)$-dimensional vector $\mathbf{s}=(s_0, s_1, \ldots, s_{l})\in S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l$, let \begin{align*} R(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \bigl\{ \{j\in \{0\}\cup [l]: s_j=s_i\} : i\in \{0\}\cup [l]\bigr\}. \end{align*} For example, $R\bigl((a,b,a,c,d,b,f,a)\bigr)=\bigl\{\{0,2,7\}, \{1,5\}, \{3\}, \{4\}, \{6\}\bigr\}$. Note that $R(\mathbf{s})$ is a partition of $\{0\}\cup [l]$. From the definition, we have $|R(\mathbf{s})|=|U(\mathbf{s})|$. For example, $|U\bigl((a,b,a,c,d,b,f,a)\bigr)|=|\{a,b,c,d,f\}|=5=|R\bigl((a,b,a,c,d,b,f,a)\bigr)|$. Let $\mathcal{R}_l$ be the family of all partitions of $\{0\}\cup [l]$. For example, \begin{align*} \mathcal{R}_2 &= \Bigl\{ \bigl\{ \{0\},\{1\},\{2\} \bigr\}, \bigl\{ \{0\},\{1,2\} \bigr\}, \bigl\{ \{1\},\{0,2\} \bigr\}, \bigl\{ \{2\},\{0,1\} \bigr\}, \bigl\{ \{0,1,2\} \bigr\} \Bigr\}. \end{align*}

Then we have \begin{align} \sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \prod_{i=0}^l S_i:\\ |U(\mathbf{s})| \leq k+1}}p^{|U(\mathbf{s})|} &=\sum_{\substack{R\in \mathcal{R}_{l}:\\|R|\leq k+1}}\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \prod_{i=0}^l S_i: \\ R(\mathbf{s})=R}}p^{|U(\mathbf{s})|} =\sum_{\substack{R\in \mathcal{R}_{l}:\\|R|\leq k+1}}p^{|R|}\left|\left\{\mathbf{s}\in \prod_{i=0}^l S_i: R(\mathbf{s})=R\right\}\right|. \end{align}

From the definition of $R(\mathbf{s})$, for any $r \in R(\mathbf{s})$, $s_i=s_j$ for any $i,j \in r$. nodes.name: Blocks of $L$
nodes.statement: For an index $i\in \{0\}\cup [l]$, let $r_i$ be the element of $R$ such that $r_i\ni i$. Now let us consider the set $L$ described in the statement (of \cref{lem:technique}).

nodes.name: Two $L$-indices share a block
nodes.statement: First we assume that there exist $i,j\in L$ with $i\neq j$ such that both $i$ and $j$ in the same $r_*=r_i=r_j\in R$. In this case, since $S_i\cap S_j=\emptyset$ from the definition of $L$, we have \begin{align} \prod_{r\in R}\left|\bigcap_{i\in r}S_i\right|=\left|\bigcap_{i\in r_*}S_i\right|\prod_{r\in R\setminus r_*}\left|\bigcap_{i\in r}S_i\right|=0. \end{align}

nodes.statement: Now we assume that $r_i\neq r_j$ for any $i, j\in L$. Then since $|\{r_i: i\in L\}|=|L|$ and $R=\{r_i: i\in L\} \cup R\setminus \{r_i: i\in L\}$, we have \begin{align} \prod_{r\in R}\left|\bigcap_{i\in r}S_i\right| =\prod_{i\in L}\left|\bigcap_{j\in r_i}S_j\right|\prod_{r\in R\setminus \{r_i: i\in L\}}\left|\bigcap_{j\in r}S_j\right| \leq \left(\prod_{i\in L}|S_i|\right) N^{|R|-|L|}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Finally, by combining \cref{eqn:C2_1,eqn:C2_2,eqn:C2_4,eq:equivalenceexample1,eqn:C2_5}, we obtain \begin{align*} \sum_{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|} &\leq \frac{1}{p}\sum_{\substack{R\in \mathcal{R}_{l}:\\|R|\leq k+1}}p^{|R|}\left|\left\{\mathbf{s}\in \prod_{i=0}^l S_i: R(\mathbf{s})=R\right\}\right| \\ &\leq \frac{1}{p}\sum_{\substack{R\in \mathcal{R}_{l}:\\|R|\leq k+1}} p^{|R|} N^{|R|}\frac{\prod_{i\in L}|S_{i}|}{N^{|L|}} \leq \frac{1}{p}\left(\frac{\prod_{i\in L}|S_{i}|}{N^{|L|}}\right) (N p)^{k+1} \sum_{\substack{R\in \mathcal{R}_{l}:\\|R|\leq k+1}} 1\\ &\leq |\mathcal{R}_{l}| \left(\frac{\prod_{i\in l}|S_{i}|}{N^{|L|}}\right) N (N p)^k = \mathcal{B}_{l+1}\left(\frac{\prod_{i\in L}|S_{i}|}{N^{|L|}}\right) N (N p)^k. \end{align*} Note that the third inequality follows since $N p\geq 1$ from the assumption.

nodes.name: Degree concentration in $G(2n,p,q)$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $0\leq q\leq p=\omega(\log n/n)$. Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that $G(2n,p,q)$ satisfies the following with probability $1-O(n^{-C_1})$: \begin{align*} \forall v\in V: |\deg(v)-n(p+q)|\leq C_2\sqrt{np\log n}. \end{align*}
conclusions: two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that $G(2n,p,q)$ satisfies the following with probability $1-O(n^{-C_1})$:
nodes.label: lem:maxmindegree

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.5
nodes.statement: Applying the Chernoff bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:chernoff-additive}), \begin{align*} \lefteqn{ \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\exists v\in V: |\deg(v)-n(p+q)|> t\right]}\\ &\leq \sum_{v\in V}\left(\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{3\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]}\right)+\exp\left(-\frac{t}{3}\right)+\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]}\right)\right)\\ &\leq n\left(2\exp\left(-\frac{t^2}{6np}\right)+ \exp\left(-\frac{t}{3}\right)\right)\\ &\leq 2\exp\left(\log n-\frac{t^2}{6np}\right)+ \exp\left(\log n-\frac{t}{3}\right). \end{align*} Note that $\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]=(n-1)p+nq$ for any $v\in V$ and $\mathbf{E}[\deg(v)]\leq n(p+q)\leq 2np$. Thus we obtain the claim letting $t=C_2\sqrt{np\log n}$ since $ t =C_2\sqrt{np\log n} \geq C\log n $ for some constant $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Additive Chernoff bound for each degree plus a union bound over vertices with $t=C_2\sqrt{np\log n}$.

For any constant $\ell$, two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that $G(2n,p,q)$ satisfies the following with probability $1-O(n^{-C_1})$: \begin{align*} \lefteqn{\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):}\\ &\bigl|W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)-\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\bigr|\leq C_2 |A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align*}

nodes.statement: First we claim the following: Two positive constants $C_3, C_4$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-n^{-C_3}$: \begin{align} &\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):\nonumber \\ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\geq \hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)-C_4|A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align}

nodes.statement: From Janson's inequality (\cref{lem:Janson}) and \cref{claim:nablaupper} with a constant $C_5$ and $C_6=\sqrt{2(C_5+1)\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}}$, we have \begin{align} &\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[ \substack{\exists A\subseteq V, \\ \exists S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A)}: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\leq \mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)] -C_6|A|\sqrt{\log N}(Np)^{\ell-1/2} \right] \nonumber \\ &\leq \binom{N}{|A|} |\mathcal{S}(A)|^\ell \exp\left(-\frac{2(C_5+1)\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|A| (\log N) (Np)^{2\ell-1}}{2\mathcal{B}_{2(\ell+1)}|A|(Np)^{2\ell-1}}\right) \nonumber \\ & \leq 9^\ell \exp\left(|A|\log N-(C_5+1)|A|\log N\right) \leq 9^\ell/N^{C_5}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Upper bound.} Now we show the following claim: Two positive constants $C_7, C_8$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-n^{-C_7}$: \begin{align} &\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):\nonumber \\ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\leq \hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)+C_8|A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align} From the same discussion of \eqref{eq:WdlV}, \begin{align} W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A) &=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A)-\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell-1},A) \end{align} since $W_{\ell}-W_0=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}(W_{i+1}-W_{i})$. Thus we consider an upper bound on $W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)$. Let $d_{\max}\mathrel{\mathop:}= \max_{v\in V}\deg(v)$. Since $\sum_{v\in V}\deg_A(v)=\sum_{a\in A}\deg(v)$, we have \begin{align*} W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A) &=\sum_{v\in V}\deg(v)^{\ell-1}\deg_A(v) \leq d_{\max}^{\ell-1}\sum_{v\in V}\deg_A(v) \leq d_{\max}^{\ell-1}\sum_{a\in A}\deg(a) \leq d_{\max}^{\ell}|A|. \end{align*} From \cref{lem:maxmindegree}, it holds with high probability that \begin{align*} d_{\max}^\ell &=\left(n(p+q)+O(\sqrt{np\log n})\right)^{\ell} =\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^\ell \left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right). \end{align*} The second equality holds since $(\log n)/(np)=o(1)$ and $\ell$ is a constant. Hence we have \begin{align} W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A) &\leq d_{\max}^{\ell}|A| =|A|\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^\ell \left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right) \nonumber \\ &\leq \hat{W}(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A)+O(|A|\sqrt{\log n} (np)^{\ell-1/2}). \end{align} Note that $\hat{W}(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell},A)=|A|\bigl((n-1)p+nq\bigr)^{\ell}$. Thus we obtain the claim \cref{claim:gomiAupper} by applying \cref{eq:gomiAlast,claim:gomiAlower} to \cref{eq:gimiAsum}. Combining the claims \cref{claim:gomiAupper,claim:gomiAlower} complete the proof of \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy2}.

nodes.name: Claim (36)
nodes.statement: Now we show the following claim: Two positive constants $C_7, C_8$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-n^{-C_7}$: \begin{align} &\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):\nonumber \\ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\leq \hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)+C_8|A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Uniform upper bound on $W(\dots,A)$
nodes.statement: &\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):\nonumber \\ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\leq \hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)+C_8|A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}.
conclusions: &\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):\nonumber \\ &W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\leq \hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)+C_8|A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}.
nodes.label: claim:gomiAupper

nodes.name: Telescoping
nodes.statement: From the same discussion of \eqref{eq:WdlV}, \begin{align} W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A) &=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A)-\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell-1},A) \end{align} since $W_{\ell}-W_0=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}(W_{i+1}-W_{i})$. Thus we consider an upper bound on $W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)$.

nodes.name: Telescoping identity with $A$
nodes.statement: W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A) &=W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A)-\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{i},V\setminus S_{i}, S_{i+1}, \ldots, S_{\ell-1},A)
nodes.label: eq:gimiAsum

nodes.name: Max-degree bound
nodes.statement: Let $d_{\max}\mathrel{\mathop:}= \max_{v\in V}\deg(v)$. Since $\sum_{v\in V}\deg_A(v)=\sum_{a\in A}\deg(v)$, we have \begin{align*} W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A) &=\sum_{v\in V}\deg(v)^{\ell-1}\deg_A(v) \leq d_{\max}^{\ell-1}\sum_{v\in V}\deg_A(v) \leq d_{\max}^{\ell-1}\sum_{a\in A}\deg(a) \leq d_{\max}^{\ell}|A|. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Degree concentration
nodes.statement: From \cref{lem:maxmindegree}, it holds with high probability that \begin{align*} d_{\max}^\ell &=\left(n(p+q)+O(\sqrt{np\log n})\right)^{\ell} =\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^\ell \left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right). \end{align*} The second equality holds since $(\log n)/(np)=o(1)$ and $\ell$ is a constant.

Hence we have \begin{align} W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A) &\leq d_{\max}^{\ell}|A| =|A|\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^\ell \left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right) \nonumber \\ &\leq \hat{W}(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A)+O(|A|\sqrt{\log n} (np)^{\ell-1/2}). \end{align} Note that $\hat{W}(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots,V}^{\ell},A)=|A|\bigl((n-1)p+nq\bigr)^{\ell}$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $W(V;\dots,V,A)$
nodes.statement: W(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A) &\leq d_{\max}^{\ell}|A| =|A|\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^\ell \left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right) \nonumber \\ &\leq \hat{W}(\overbrace{V;V,\ldots, V}^{\ell},A)+O(|A|\sqrt{\log n} (np)^{\ell-1/2}).
nodes.label: eq:gomiAlast

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus we obtain the claim \cref{claim:gomiAupper} by applying \cref{eq:gomiAlast,claim:gomiAlower} to \cref{eq:gimiAsum}. Combining the claims \cref{claim:gomiAupper,claim:gomiAlower} complete the proof of \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy2}.

nodes.name: Proof of (P3) of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement: Let $d_{\min}\mathrel{\mathop:}= \min_{v\in V}\deg(v)$. Then for any $j\in [\ell]$, \begin{align*} \sum_{s\in S\cap V_i}\left(\frac{\deg_A(s)}{\deg(s)}\right)^j &\leq d_{\min}^{-j}\sum_{s\in S\cap V_i}\deg_A(s)^j =d_{\min}^{-j}W(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j}). \end{align*} From \cref{lem:maxmindegree}, it holds with high probability that \begin{align*} d_{\min}^{-j} &=\left(n(p+q)-O(\sqrt{np\log n})\right)^{-j} =\left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right)\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^{-j}. \end{align*} The second equality holds since $(\log n)/(np)=o(1)$ and $j\in [\ell]$ is a constant. Thus from \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy2}, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{s\in S\cap V_i}\left(\frac{\deg_A(s)}{\deg(s)}\right)^j &=\left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\hat{W}(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j})}{(n(p+q))^j}+O\left(|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right)\\ &\leq |S\cap V_i|\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right)^j+O\left(|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right). \end{align*} Note that $\frac{|S\cap V_i|(|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q)^{j}}{(n(p+q))^j}= \frac{|S\cap V_i|(|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q)}{n(p+q)}\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right)^{j-1}\leq\frac{|A|p}{(p+q)}\leq |A|$. Thus we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Bound degree ratios by $d_{\min}^{-j}W(S\cap V_i;A,\dots,A)$, control $d_{\min}$ by Lemma 8.5 and $W$ by Lemma 8.6.

nodes.name: Min-degree reduction
nodes.statement: Let $d_{\min}\mathrel{\mathop:}= \min_{v\in V}\deg(v)$. Then for any $j\in [\ell]$, \begin{align*} \sum_{s\in S\cap V_i}\left(\frac{\deg_A(s)}{\deg(s)}\right)^j &\leq d_{\min}^{-j}\sum_{s\in S\cap V_i}\deg_A(s)^j =d_{\min}^{-j}W(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j}). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Degree concentration
nodes.statement: From \cref{lem:maxmindegree}, it holds with high probability that \begin{align*} d_{\min}^{-j} &=\left(n(p+q)-O(\sqrt{np\log n})\right)^{-j} =\left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right)\bigl(n(p+q)\bigr)^{-j}. \end{align*} The second equality holds since $(\log n)/(np)=o(1)$ and $j\in [\ell]$ is a constant.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 8.6
nodes.statement: Thus from \cref{lem:WIdiscrepancy2}, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{s\in S\cap V_i}\left(\frac{\deg_A(s)}{\deg(s)}\right)^j &=\left(1+O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\hat{W}(S\cap V_i;\overbrace{A,\ldots,A}^{j})}{(n(p+q))^j}+O\left(|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)\right)\\ &\leq |S\cap V_i|\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right)^j+O\left(|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Replace $W$ by $\hat W$ up to $O(|A|\sqrt{\log n/np})$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Note that $\frac{|S\cap V_i|(|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q)^{j}}{(n(p+q))^j}= \frac{|S\cap V_i|(|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q)}{n(p+q)}\left(\frac{|A_i|p+|A_{3-i}|q}{n(p+q)}\right)^{j-1}\leq\frac{|A|p}{(p+q)}\leq |A|$. Thus we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: The error term is at most $|A|$ times the factor.

nodes.statement: For any $\epsilon = \omega(\sqrt{1/np})$, there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ satisfying \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\|{\boldsymbol \alpha'}-H({\boldsymbol \alpha})\|_\infty \geq\epsilon\right]\leq O(\exp(-C \epsilon^2 n)). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.2
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{x}^*$ be a sink point and $J$ be the Jacobian matrix of $H$ at $\mathbf{x}^*$. From the Taylor expansion (see, e.g.~Theorem 12.15 of \cite{Krantz16}), we have \begin{align} H(\mathbf{x})&=H(\mathbf{x}^*)+J(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*)+O_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}^*}(\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_2^2) \nonumber\\ &=\mathbf{x}^*+J(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*)+O_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}^*}(\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_2^2). \end{align} By the property of singular value (\cref{prop:singularvalue}), there exist constants $\epsilon,K>0$ such that, for any $\mathbf{x}\in B(\mathbf{x}^*,\epsilon)$, it holds that \begin{align*} \|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{x}^*\|_2&=\|H(\mathbf{x})-H(\mathbf{x}^*)\|_2 \leq \sigma_{\max}\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_2+O_{\mathbf{x}\to\mathbf{x}^*}(\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_2^2)\\ &\leq(1-K)\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_\infty <(1-K)\epsilon. \end{align*} Consequently, for any $\mathbf{y}\not\in B(\mathbf{x}^*,\epsilon)$, we have \begin{align*} \epsilon&\leq \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_\infty \leq \|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty+\|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{x}^*\|_\infty < \|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty+(1-K)\epsilon. \end{align*} Equivalently, we obtain $\|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty>K\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion at the sink and $\sigma_{\max}<1$ give $\|H(\mathbf x)-\mathbf x^*\|<(1-K)\epsilon$; triangle inequality concludes.
nodes.section: 9.1 Proof of stationary dynamics around a sink point (7.2)

nodes.statement: Consequently, for any $\mathbf{y}\not\in B(\mathbf{x}^*,\epsilon)$, we have \begin{align*} \epsilon&\leq \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}^*\|_\infty \leq \|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty+\|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{x}^*\|_\infty < \|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty+(1-K)\epsilon. \end{align*} Equivalently, we obtain $\|H(\mathbf{x})-\mathbf{y}\|_\infty>K\epsilon$.

nodes.statement: Then, \cref{lem:constantfar} implies \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[{\boldsymbol \alpha}'\not\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon) \mid {\boldsymbol \alpha}\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon)\right] &\leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}'-H({\boldsymbol \alpha})\|_\infty>K \epsilon\right]\\ &\leq \exp(-\Omega(\epsilon^2 n)). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Union bound over time
nodes.statement: For any $T$, the union bound over the time $t=1,\ldots,T$ leads to \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\exists t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}:{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}\not\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon) \,\middle|\, {\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(0)}\in B(\mathbf{a}^*,\epsilon)\right] \leq T\exp(-\Omega(\epsilon^2 n)) \end{align*} and thus, the stopping time $\tau$ satisfies $\tau\geq\exp(\Omega(\epsilon^2 n))$ w.h.p.~if $\epsilon = \omega(\max\{\sqrt{\log n/n}, \sqrt{1/np}\})$.

nodes.name: Derivation of Proposition 7.3 from Proposition 7.4
nodes.statement: It suffices to check the condition of \cref{prop:fastconsensus} for $\epsilon=\epsilon(n)=\Theta\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right)$. Using \ref{pro:gomiA} and the Taylor expansion \cref{eqn:Taylorexpansion}, there exists $C=C(H)$ such that \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A_i'|] &=n H_i(\alpha_1, \alpha_2)\pm O\left(|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right) \leq n C\left((\alpha_1+\alpha_2)^2+ |A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}}\right) \\ &=C\frac{|A|^2}{n}+ C|A|\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{np}} \end{align*} holds if $\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}\|\leq \delta$ for sufficiently small constant $\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Check the quadratic-shrinkage condition of Proposition 7.4 with $\epsilon=\Theta(\sqrt{\log n/np})$ using (P3) and the Taylor expansion at a zero-Jacobian point.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.4
nodes.statement: We prove \cref{prop:fastconsensus}. Let $n=|V(G)|$. Suppose that there exist absolute constants $C,\delta>0$ and a function $\epsilon=\epsilon(n)$ such that $\epsilon(n)=o(1)$ and $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq \frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|$ holds for all $A\subseteq V$ of $|A|\leq \delta n$. Note that we may assume $\epsilon(n)=\Omega(\sqrt{\log n/n})$: If $\epsilon=o(\sqrt{\log n/n})$, we have $\log n/\log \epsilon^{-1}=O(1)$ and we will obtain the claim by applying \cref{prop:fastconsensus} with letting $\epsilon=\sqrt{\log n/n}$. Take a positive constant $\delta'$ such that \begin{align} &10\left(\frac{CM^2}{n}+\epsilon M\right) \leq M, \\ &\delta'\leq \min\left\{\delta,\frac{1}{16C}\right\} \end{align} hold for any $0\leq M\leq \delta'n$. We can take such constant $\delta'>0$ since $\epsilon=o(1)$ and thus the inequality \cref{eqn:delta'condition1} holds if the ratio $\frac{M}{n}$ is sufficiently small. Consider $A^{(0)},A^{(1)},\ldots$ given by the voting model such that $|A^{(0)}|\leq \delta n$. To exploit the assumption of the expectation, we first claim that $|A^{(t)}|\leq \delta' n \leq \delta n$ holds w.h.p.~for all $t=0,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Let $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ be the event that $|A^{(i)}|\leq \delta n$ for all $i=0,\ldots,t$. Note that $\mathcal{B}^{(0)}$ holds. Consider $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[\mathcal{B}^{(t+1)}|\mathcal{B}^{(t)}]$. If $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\geq\log n$, the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher1} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) implies \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right) \,\middle|\, |A|\leq \delta'n\right] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq 10\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\right] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{10}{3}\log n\right) \leq n^{-3}. \end{align*} Then, for $|A|\leq \delta'n$, it holds with probability $1-O(n^{-3})$ that \begin{align} |A'|\leq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right)\leq |A|\leq\delta' n. \end{align} Here, we used \cref{eqn:delta'condition1} with letting $M=|A|$. If $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq\log n$, from the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}), we have \begin{align} |A'|\leq 6\log n =o(\delta' n) \end{align} with probability at least $1-O(n^{-3})$. From \cref{eqn:A'bound1,eqn:A'bound2}, we obtain $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\mathcal{B}^{(t+1)}\,\middle|\, \mathcal{B}^{(t)}\right]\geq 1-O(n^{-3})$ for each $t$ and thus $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ holds for $t=n^{0.01}$ with probability $1-O(n^{-2.99})$. Now we look at $|A^{(t)}|$. Note that \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A'|\mid |A|\leq \delta' n] \leq \begin{cases} \frac{2C|A|^2}{n} & \text{if $ \frac{\epsilon}{C}n \leq |A| \leq \delta'n$},\\ 2\epsilon |A| & \text{if $0\leq |A| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}$}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Thus let us consider the following two cases. \paragraph*{Case I: $\frac{\epsilon}{C}n \leq |A|^{(t)} \leq \delta'n$.} From the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}), we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A^{(t+1)}|\geq \frac{12C|A^{(t)}|^2}{n} \,\middle|\, \mathcal{B}^{(t)} \right] &\leq 2^{-\Omega(\log n)}. \end{align*} In the last inequality, we used $|A^{(t)}|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C} n = \Omega(\sqrt{n\log n})$. Hence, conditioned on $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ and $|A|^{(i)}\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ ($i=0,\ldots,t$), it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |A^{(t)}| \leq \frac{12C (|A|^{(t-1)})^2}{n} \leq \frac{n}{12C}\left(\frac{12C |A^{(0)}|}{n}\right)^{2^t} \leq \frac{0.75^{2^t}n}{12C}. \end{align*} Here, we used \cref{eqn:delta'condition2}. Therefore, for some $\tau_1=O(\log\log n)$, $|A^{(\tau_1)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}$ holds w.h.p. \paragraph*{Case I\hspace{-.1em}I: $0\leq |A^{(t)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$.} Conditioned on $|A^{(0)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$, we claim that $\mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|]\leq n^{-\Omega(1)}$ for some $\tau_2=O(\log n/\log \epsilon^{-1})$. Note that this completes the proof of \cref{prop:fastconsensus} since $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A^{(\tau_2)}\neq \emptyset]\leq \mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|]=n^{-\Omega(1)}$ from the Markov inequality. To show the claim, we exploit the property that $\mathbf{E}[|A'|\mid A]\leq 2\epsilon|A|$ if $|A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$. Before using this, we show that $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=1,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Conditioned on $|A|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$, we have $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq 2\epsilon |A| \leq O(\epsilon^2 n)$ and thus the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) yields \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n \middle| |A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n\right] \leq 2^{-\Omega(\epsilon n)} = n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*} Therefore, $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=0,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Let $\mathcal{C}^{(t)}$ be the event that $|A^{(i)}|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $i=0,\ldots,t$. Then, from the tower property of the conditional expectation, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|\mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] &\leq \mathbf{E}[\mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|\mid A^{(\tau_2-1)},\mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}]\mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] \\ &\leq \mathbf{E}[2\epsilon |A^{(\tau_2-1)}| \mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] \\ &\leq (2\epsilon)^{\tau_2} \cdot \frac{\epsilon n}{C} \\ &\leq n^{-\Omega(1)} \end{align*} for some $\tau_2=O(\log n/\log \epsilon^{-1})$. This shows the aforementioned claim as well as completes the proof of \cref{prop:fastconsensus}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $|A^{(t)}|$ stays below $\delta'n$ w.h.p.; then a doubly exponential decrease (Case I, $O(\log\log n)$ steps) followed by geometric decay of the mean by factor $2\epsilon$ (Case II) and Markov's inequality.
