nodes.name: Size stays small
nodes.statement: Consider $A^{(0)},A^{(1)},\ldots$ given by the voting model such that $|A^{(0)}|\leq \delta n$. To exploit the assumption of the expectation, we first claim that $|A^{(t)}|\leq \delta' n \leq \delta n$ holds w.h.p.~for all $t=0,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Let $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ be the event that $|A^{(i)}|\leq \delta n$ for all $i=0,\ldots,t$. Note that $\mathcal{B}^{(0)}$ holds. Consider $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[\mathcal{B}^{(t+1)}|\mathcal{B}^{(t)}]$. If $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\geq\log n$, the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher1} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) implies \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right) \,\middle|\, |A|\leq \delta'n\right] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq 10\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\right] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{10}{3}\log n\right) \leq n^{-3}. \end{align*} Then, for $|A|\leq \delta'n$, it holds with probability $1-O(n^{-3})$ that \begin{align} |A'|\leq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right)\leq |A|\leq\delta' n. \end{align} Here, we used \cref{eqn:delta'condition1} with letting $M=|A|$. If $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq\log n$, from the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}), we have \begin{align} |A'|\leq 6\log n =o(\delta' n) \end{align} with probability at least $1-O(n^{-3})$. From \cref{eqn:A'bound1,eqn:A'bound2}, we obtain $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\mathcal{B}^{(t+1)}\,\middle|\, \mathcal{B}^{(t)}\right]\geq 1-O(n^{-3})$ for each $t$ and thus $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ holds for $t=n^{0.01}$ with probability $1-O(n^{-2.99})$.

nodes.name: Event $\mathcal B^{(t)}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ be the event that $|A^{(i)}|\leq \delta n$ for all $i=0,\ldots,t$. Note that $\mathcal{B}^{(0)}$ holds. Consider $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[\mathcal{B}^{(t+1)}|\mathcal{B}^{(t)}]$.

nodes.name: Large mean
nodes.statement: If $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\geq\log n$, the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher1} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) implies \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right) \,\middle|\, |A|\leq \delta'n\right] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq 10\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\right] \leq \exp\left(-\frac{10}{3}\log n\right) \leq n^{-3}. \end{align*} Then, for $|A|\leq \delta'n$, it holds with probability $1-O(n^{-3})$ that \begin{align} |A'|\leq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right)\leq |A|\leq\delta' n. \end{align} Here, we used \cref{eqn:delta'condition1} with letting $M=|A|$.

nodes.name: One-step bound for $|A'|$ (large mean)
nodes.statement: |A'|\leq 10\left(\frac{C|A|^2}{n}+\epsilon|A|\right)\leq |A|\leq\delta' n.
nodes.label: eqn:A'bound1

nodes.name: Small mean
nodes.statement: If $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq\log n$, from the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}), we have \begin{align} |A'|\leq 6\log n =o(\delta' n) \end{align} with probability at least $1-O(n^{-3})$.

nodes.name: One-step bound for $|A'|$ (small mean)
nodes.statement: |A'|\leq 6\log n =o(\delta' n)
nodes.label: eqn:A'bound2

nodes.name: Union over time
nodes.statement: From \cref{eqn:A'bound1,eqn:A'bound2}, we obtain $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\mathcal{B}^{(t+1)}\,\middle|\, \mathcal{B}^{(t)}\right]\geq 1-O(n^{-3})$ for each $t$ and thus $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ holds for $t=n^{0.01}$ with probability $1-O(n^{-2.99})$.
nodes.statement_short: The good event holds for $n^{0.01}$ steps.

nodes.name: Two regimes
nodes.statement: Now we look at $|A^{(t)}|$. Note that \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A'|\mid |A|\leq \delta' n] \leq \begin{cases} \frac{2C|A|^2}{n} & \text{if $ \frac{\epsilon}{C}n \leq |A| \leq \delta'n$},\\ 2\epsilon |A| & \text{if $0\leq |A| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}$}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Thus let us consider the following two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Split by the size of $|A|$ relative to $\epsilon n/C$.

nodes.name: Case I: large $|A|$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Case I: $\frac{\epsilon}{C}n \leq |A|^{(t)} \leq \delta'n$.} From the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}), we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A^{(t+1)}|\geq \frac{12C|A^{(t)}|^2}{n} \,\middle|\, \mathcal{B}^{(t)} \right] &\leq 2^{-\Omega(\log n)}. \end{align*} In the last inequality, we used $|A^{(t)}|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C} n = \Omega(\sqrt{n\log n})$. Hence, conditioned on $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ and $|A|^{(i)}\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ ($i=0,\ldots,t$), it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |A^{(t)}| \leq \frac{12C (|A|^{(t-1)})^2}{n} \leq \frac{n}{12C}\left(\frac{12C |A^{(0)}|}{n}\right)^{2^t} \leq \frac{0.75^{2^t}n}{12C}. \end{align*} Here, we used \cref{eqn:delta'condition2}. Therefore, for some $\tau_1=O(\log\log n)$, $|A^{(\tau_1)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic shrinkage reaches $\epsilon n/C$ in $O(\log\log n)$ steps.

nodes.name: Chernoff
nodes.statement: From the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}), we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A^{(t+1)}|\geq \frac{12C|A^{(t)}|^2}{n} \,\middle|\, \mathcal{B}^{(t)} \right] &\leq 2^{-\Omega(\log n)}. \end{align*} In the last inequality, we used $|A^{(t)}|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C} n = \Omega(\sqrt{n\log n})$.

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement: Hence, conditioned on $\mathcal{B}^{(t)}$ and $|A|^{(i)}\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ ($i=0,\ldots,t$), it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |A^{(t)}| \leq \frac{12C (|A|^{(t-1)})^2}{n} \leq \frac{n}{12C}\left(\frac{12C |A^{(0)}|}{n}\right)^{2^t} \leq \frac{0.75^{2^t}n}{12C}. \end{align*} Here, we used \cref{eqn:delta'condition2}.

nodes.name: Conclude Case I
nodes.statement: Therefore, for some $\tau_1=O(\log\log n)$, $|A^{(\tau_1)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}$ holds w.h.p.

nodes.name: Case II: small $|A|$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Case I\hspace{-.1em}I: $0\leq |A^{(t)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$.} Conditioned on $|A^{(0)}| \leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$, we claim that $\mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|]\leq n^{-\Omega(1)}$ for some $\tau_2=O(\log n/\log \epsilon^{-1})$. Note that this completes the proof of \cref{prop:fastconsensus} since $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A^{(\tau_2)}\neq \emptyset]\leq \mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|]=n^{-\Omega(1)}$ from the Markov inequality. To show the claim, we exploit the property that $\mathbf{E}[|A'|\mid A]\leq 2\epsilon|A|$ if $|A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$. Before using this, we show that $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=1,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Conditioned on $|A|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$, we have $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq 2\epsilon |A| \leq O(\epsilon^2 n)$ and thus the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) yields \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n \middle| |A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n\right] \leq 2^{-\Omega(\epsilon n)} = n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*} Therefore, $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=0,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Let $\mathcal{C}^{(t)}$ be the event that $|A^{(i)}|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $i=0,\ldots,t$. Then, from the tower property of the conditional expectation, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|\mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] &\leq \mathbf{E}[\mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|\mid A^{(\tau_2-1)},\mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}]\mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] \\ &\leq \mathbf{E}[2\epsilon |A^{(\tau_2-1)}| \mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] \\ &\leq (2\epsilon)^{\tau_2} \cdot \frac{\epsilon n}{C} \\ &\leq n^{-\Omega(1)} \end{align*} for some $\tau_2=O(\log n/\log \epsilon^{-1})$. This shows the aforementioned claim as well as completes the proof of \cref{prop:fastconsensus}.
nodes.statement_short: Expected size decays by factor $2\epsilon$ per step; Markov's inequality.

nodes.name: Markov
nodes.statement: Note that this completes the proof of \cref{prop:fastconsensus} since $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A^{(\tau_2)}\neq \emptyset]\leq \mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|]=n^{-\Omega(1)}$ from the Markov inequality.
nodes.statement_short: The claim implies the proposition by Markov's inequality.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: To show the claim, we exploit the property that $\mathbf{E}[|A'|\mid A]\leq 2\epsilon|A|$ if $|A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$.

nodes.name: Size stays below $\epsilon n/C$
nodes.statement: Before using this, we show that $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=1,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$. Conditioned on $|A|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$, we have $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq 2\epsilon |A| \leq O(\epsilon^2 n)$ and thus the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) yields \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n \middle| |A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n\right] \leq 2^{-\Omega(\epsilon n)} = n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*} Therefore, $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=0,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$.

nodes.name: Chernoff
nodes.statement: Conditioned on $|A|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$, we have $\mathbf{E}[|A'|]\leq 2\epsilon |A| \leq O(\epsilon^2 n)$ and thus the Chernoff bound (\ref{eqn:cher3} of \cref{lem:chernoff}) yields \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|A'|\geq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n \middle| |A|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n\right] \leq 2^{-\Omega(\epsilon n)} = n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: All steps
nodes.statement: Therefore, $|A^{(t)}|\leq \frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $t=0,\ldots,n^{o(1)}$.

nodes.name: Tower property
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}^{(t)}$ be the event that $|A^{(i)}|\leq\frac{\epsilon}{C}n$ holds for all $i=0,\ldots,t$. Then, from the tower property of the conditional expectation, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|\mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] &\leq \mathbf{E}[\mathbf{E}[|A^{(\tau_2)}|\mid A^{(\tau_2-1)},\mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}]\mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] \\ &\leq \mathbf{E}[2\epsilon |A^{(\tau_2-1)}| \mid \mathcal{C}^{(\tau_2)}] \\ &\leq (2\epsilon)^{\tau_2} \cdot \frac{\epsilon n}{C} \\ &\leq n^{-\Omega(1)} \end{align*} for some $\tau_2=O(\log n/\log \epsilon^{-1})$. This shows the aforementioned claim as well as completes the proof of \cref{prop:fastconsensus}.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.8
nodes.statement_short: Work in eigen-coordinates $\boldsymbol\beta$ with $|\beta'_i|\approx|\lambda_i||\beta_i|$; move through regions $\mathcal A_1\to\mathcal A_2\to\mathcal A_3$ (or $\mathcal B_1,\dots,\mathcal B_4$), using Berry-Esseen and the drift corollary A.13 to break symmetry from $O(\sqrt{\log n/n})$ scale.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: In this section, we prove \cref{prop:escape}. Let $\mathbf{a}^*$ be a fixed point satisfying \cref{asm:escape_assumption0}. The proof of \cref{prop:escape} consists of two parts: We derive \cref{prop:escape} from \cref{asm:escape_assumption1,asm:escape_assumption2}.
nodes.statement_short: Two parts: under Assumption 7.6 and under Assumption 7.7.

nodes.name: Dynamics of $\boldsymbol\beta$
nodes.statement: Recall the random variable ${\boldsymbol \beta}$ defined in \cref{eqn:betadef}. From the definition \cref{eqn:betadef}, each element $\beta_i$ of ${\boldsymbol \beta}$ can be rewritten as \begin{align} \beta_i&=\sum_{j=1}^2 u_{ij} \alpha_j-(U\mathbf{a}^*)_i, \end{align} where we let $U=(u_{ij})$. Each element $u_{ij}$ of the matrix $U$ does not depend on $n$. Hence, the Hoeffding bound (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}) implies \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[|\beta'_i-\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq t]\leq \exp\left(-\Omega(t^2n)\right). \end{align} From \cref{thm:approximation_vectorfield} and the Taylor expansion \cref{eqn:Taylorexpansion}, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[{\boldsymbol \beta}' \mid A] &= \mathbf{E}[U({\boldsymbol \alpha}'-\mathbf{a}^*) \mid A]\\ &=U(H({\boldsymbol \alpha})-\mathbf{a}^*)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right)\cdot \mathbf{1}\\ &=UJ({\boldsymbol \alpha}-\mathbf{a}^*)+\left(O_{{\boldsymbol \alpha}\to \mathbf{a}^*}(\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}-\mathbf{a}^*\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right)\right)\cdot \mathbf{1}\\ &=\Lambda {\boldsymbol \beta}+\left(O_{\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|\to 0}(\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right)\right)\cdot \mathbf{1}. \end{align*} Hence, the $i$-th element $\beta_i$ of ${\boldsymbol \beta}=(\beta_1\,\beta_2)^{\top}$ satisfies \begin{align} |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]| = |\lambda_i\|\beta_i|+O_{\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|\to 0}(\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right). \end{align} It is convenient to consider the behavior of ${\boldsymbol \beta}$ instead of ${\boldsymbol \alpha}$. Note that ${\boldsymbol \alpha}\to \mathbf{a}^*$ implies ${\boldsymbol \beta}\to \mathbf{0}$ and vice versa since the matrix $U$ is nonsingular. By substituting $t=\Theta\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)$ to \cref{eqn:beta_concentration}, for sufficiently large constant $C>0$, it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align} \left| |\beta'_i| - |\lambda_i||\beta_i| \right| \leq C\|{\boldmath \beta}\|_{\infty}^2+ C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Linear form
nodes.statement: Recall the random variable ${\boldsymbol \beta}$ defined in \cref{eqn:betadef}. From the definition \cref{eqn:betadef}, each element $\beta_i$ of ${\boldsymbol \beta}$ can be rewritten as \begin{align} \beta_i&=\sum_{j=1}^2 u_{ij} \alpha_j-(U\mathbf{a}^*)_i, \end{align} where we let $U=(u_{ij})$. Each element $u_{ij}$ of the matrix $U$ does not depend on $n$.

nodes.name: $\beta_i$ as a linear function of $\alpha$
nodes.statement: \beta_i&=\sum_{j=1}^2 u_{ij} \alpha_j-(U\mathbf{a}^*)_i,
nodes.label: eqn:beta_sum_of_irv

nodes.name: Hoeffding
nodes.statement: Hence, the Hoeffding bound (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}) implies \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[|\beta'_i-\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq t]\leq \exp\left(-\Omega(t^2n)\right). \end{align}

nodes.name: Concentration of $\beta'_i$
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[|\beta'_i-\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq t]\leq \exp\left(-\Omega(t^2n)\right).
nodes.label: eqn:beta_concentration

nodes.name: Expected update
nodes.statement: From \cref{thm:approximation_vectorfield} and the Taylor expansion \cref{eqn:Taylorexpansion}, we have \begin{align*} \mathbf{E}[{\boldsymbol \beta}' \mid A] &= \mathbf{E}[U({\boldsymbol \alpha}'-\mathbf{a}^*) \mid A]\\ &=U(H({\boldsymbol \alpha})-\mathbf{a}^*)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right)\cdot \mathbf{1}\\ &=UJ({\boldsymbol \alpha}-\mathbf{a}^*)+\left(O_{{\boldsymbol \alpha}\to \mathbf{a}^*}(\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}-\mathbf{a}^*\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right)\right)\cdot \mathbf{1}\\ &=\Lambda {\boldsymbol \beta}+\left(O_{\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|\to 0}(\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right)\right)\cdot \mathbf{1}. \end{align*} Hence, the $i$-th element $\beta_i$ of ${\boldsymbol \beta}=(\beta_1\,\beta_2)^{\top}$ satisfies \begin{align} |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]| = |\lambda_i\|\beta_i|+O_{\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|\to 0}(\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right). \end{align}

nodes.name: Expected update of $\beta_i$
nodes.statement: |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]| = |\lambda_i\|\beta_i|+O_{\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|\to 0}(\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty^2)+O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}\right).
nodes.label: eqn:exp_beta'

nodes.name: Equivalence
nodes.statement: It is convenient to consider the behavior of ${\boldsymbol \beta}$ instead of ${\boldsymbol \alpha}$. Note that ${\boldsymbol \alpha}\to \mathbf{a}^*$ implies ${\boldsymbol \beta}\to \mathbf{0}$ and vice versa since the matrix $U$ is nonsingular.

By substituting $t=\Theta\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)$ to \cref{eqn:beta_concentration}, for sufficiently large constant $C>0$, it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align} \left| |\beta'_i| - |\lambda_i||\beta_i| \right| \leq C\|{\boldmath \beta}\|_{\infty}^2+ C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Two-sided bound on $|\beta'_i|$
nodes.statement: \left| |\beta'_i| - |\lambda_i||\beta_i| \right| \leq C\|{\boldmath \beta}\|_{\infty}^2+ C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}.
nodes.label: eqn:beta'bounds

nodes.name: Under Assumption 7.6
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Derive \cref{prop:escape} from \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}} Suppose that the fixed point $\mathbf{a}^*$ satisfies \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}. Let $I_{>1} \mathrel{\mathop:}= \{i\in[2]:|\lambda_i|>1\}$ and $I_{\leq 1} \mathrel{\mathop:}= [2]\setminus I_{>1}$. Fix a sufficiently large constant $K>0$ and let $\epsilon^*$ be the constant mentioned in \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}. Define \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_1&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon^* \text{ and }|\beta_j|< K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \text{ for all }j\in I_{>1} \right\},\\ \mathcal{A}_2&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon^* \text{ and }|\beta_j|\geq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \text{ for some }j\in I_{>1} \right\},\\ \mathcal{A}_3&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty >\epsilon^* \text{ and }|\beta_j|\leq \epsilon^* \text{ for all }j\in I_{\leq 1} \right\}. \end{align*} We claim that, for each $i=1,2$ and any $A\in \mathcal{A}_i$, there exists $\tau=O(\log n)$ satisfying $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_{i+1}\,\middle| A^{(0)}=A \right] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)}$. This completes the proof of \cref{prop:escape} under \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}. \paragraph*{Case I: $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{A}_1$.} Let $f(A)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \lfloor n\max\{|\beta_i|:i\in I_{>1}\}\rfloor$ and $m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$. We use \cref{cor:nazocor} to show $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$ for some $\tau=O(\log n)$. Here, we use $\mathcal{A}_1$ as $\mathcal{B}$ of \cref{cor:nazocor}. Note that $A\in\mathcal{A}_1$ implies $f(A)<m$. From \cref{eqn:beta_sum_of_irv} and \ref{asm:asm2}, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|\beta_i| \mid A]=\sum_{j\in[2]} u_{ij}^2 \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha_j \mid A]=\Omega(n^{-1})$. Here, note that, for every $i\in[2]$, there exists $j\in[2]$ such that $u_{ij}\neq 0$, since otherwise, it contradicts to the fact that the matrix $U$ is nonsingular. Thus, from \cref{cor:BEbound_cor}, it holds that, for any constant $h>0$, there exists a positive constant $C_1<1$ such that $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')< h\sqrt{n} \mid f(A)\leq m] < C_1.$ This verifies the condition~\ref{cond:nazo_sqrt} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. Now we check the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff}. Let $z\in[2]$ be the least index satisfying $|\beta_z|=\max\{|\beta_i|:i\in[2]\}$. Suppose that $A\in \mathcal{A}_1$ satisfies $f(A)=\lfloor n|\beta_z|\rfloor \geq h\sqrt{n}$ for sufficiently large constant $h>\frac{100 C}{\epsilon_1}$ (recall that the constant $\epsilon_1$ is mentioned in \ref{asm:asm4}). Then, from \ref{asm:asm4}, we have \begin{align*} |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_z \mid A]| &\geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_z| + 0.01\epsilon_1|\beta_z|-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}} \geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_z|. \end{align*} Thus, from the Hoeffding inequality (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}), we obtain \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')<(1+0.98\epsilon_1)f(A) \mid A] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[f(A')<\frac{1+0.98\epsilon_1}{1+0.99\epsilon_1}\mathbf{E}[f(A')]\,\middle|\,A\right] \leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right) \end{align*} holds for every $A\in \mathcal{A}_1$ satisfying $f(A)\geq h\sqrt{n}$. This verifies the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff}. Finally, we check the condition~\ref{cond:whp} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. From \ref{asm:asm5}, it holds that \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A'\not\in \mathcal{A}_1\text{ and }f(A')<m \mid A\in \mathcal{A}_1] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[\exists j\in I_{\leq 1},|\beta'_j|>\epsilon^* \mid A\in\mathcal{A}_1] \leq n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*} Therefore, from \cref{cor:nazocor}, we have $f(A^{(\tau)})\geq m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$ (i.e.~$A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$) holds w.h.p.~for some $\tau=O(\log n)$. \paragraph*{Case I\hspace{-.1em}I: $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$.} Suppose that $A^{(0)}\in\mathcal{A}_2$ and let $j\in I_{>1}$ be the index satisfying $|\beta_j|>K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$. We remark that $K$ is sufficiently large. From \ref{asm:asm4} and \cref{eqn:beta'bounds}, we have $|\beta'_j|\geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_j|$. Thus, for some $\tau=O(\log n)$, we have $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j|>\epsilon^*$. Moreover, from \ref{asm:asm5}, we have $|\beta^{(\tau)}_i|\leq\epsilon^*$ for all $i\in I_{\leq 1}$. Therefore, $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_3$ holds w.h.p.

nodes.name: Regions $\mathcal A_i$
nodes.statement: Suppose that the fixed point $\mathbf{a}^*$ satisfies \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}. Let $I_{>1} \mathrel{\mathop:}= \{i\in[2]:|\lambda_i|>1\}$ and $I_{\leq 1} \mathrel{\mathop:}= [2]\setminus I_{>1}$. Fix a sufficiently large constant $K>0$ and let $\epsilon^*$ be the constant mentioned in \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}. Define \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_1&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon^* \text{ and }|\beta_j|< K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \text{ for all }j\in I_{>1} \right\},\\ \mathcal{A}_2&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon^* \text{ and }|\beta_j|\geq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \text{ for some }j\in I_{>1} \right\},\\ \mathcal{A}_3&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty >\epsilon^* \text{ and }|\beta_j|\leq \epsilon^* \text{ for all }j\in I_{\leq 1} \right\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define $I_{>1},I_{\le1}$ and regions $\mathcal A_1,\mathcal A_2,\mathcal A_3$.

nodes.name: Claim
nodes.statement: We claim that, for each $i=1,2$ and any $A\in \mathcal{A}_i$, there exists $\tau=O(\log n)$ satisfying $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_{i+1}\,\middle| A^{(0)}=A \right] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)}$. This completes the proof of \cref{prop:escape} under \cref{asm:escape_assumption1}.
nodes.statement_short: Each region is left for the next in $O(\log n)$ steps.

nodes.name: Case I: $\mathcal A_1$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Case I: $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{A}_1$.} Let $f(A)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \lfloor n\max\{|\beta_i|:i\in I_{>1}\}\rfloor$ and $m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$. We use \cref{cor:nazocor} to show $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$ for some $\tau=O(\log n)$. Here, we use $\mathcal{A}_1$ as $\mathcal{B}$ of \cref{cor:nazocor}. Note that $A\in\mathcal{A}_1$ implies $f(A)<m$. From \cref{eqn:beta_sum_of_irv} and \ref{asm:asm2}, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|\beta_i| \mid A]=\sum_{j\in[2]} u_{ij}^2 \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha_j \mid A]=\Omega(n^{-1})$. Here, note that, for every $i\in[2]$, there exists $j\in[2]$ such that $u_{ij}\neq 0$, since otherwise, it contradicts to the fact that the matrix $U$ is nonsingular. Thus, from \cref{cor:BEbound_cor}, it holds that, for any constant $h>0$, there exists a positive constant $C_1<1$ such that $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')< h\sqrt{n} \mid f(A)\leq m] < C_1.$ This verifies the condition~\ref{cond:nazo_sqrt} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. Now we check the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff}. Let $z\in[2]$ be the least index satisfying $|\beta_z|=\max\{|\beta_i|:i\in[2]\}$. Suppose that $A\in \mathcal{A}_1$ satisfies $f(A)=\lfloor n|\beta_z|\rfloor \geq h\sqrt{n}$ for sufficiently large constant $h>\frac{100 C}{\epsilon_1}$ (recall that the constant $\epsilon_1$ is mentioned in \ref{asm:asm4}). Then, from \ref{asm:asm4}, we have \begin{align*} |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_z \mid A]| &\geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_z| + 0.01\epsilon_1|\beta_z|-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}} \geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_z|. \end{align*} Thus, from the Hoeffding inequality (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}), we obtain \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')<(1+0.98\epsilon_1)f(A) \mid A] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[f(A')<\frac{1+0.98\epsilon_1}{1+0.99\epsilon_1}\mathbf{E}[f(A')]\,\middle|\,A\right] \leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right) \end{align*} holds for every $A\in \mathcal{A}_1$ satisfying $f(A)\geq h\sqrt{n}$. This verifies the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff}. Finally, we check the condition~\ref{cond:whp} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. From \ref{asm:asm5}, it holds that \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A'\not\in \mathcal{A}_1\text{ and }f(A')<m \mid A\in \mathcal{A}_1] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[\exists j\in I_{\leq 1},|\beta'_j|>\epsilon^* \mid A\in\mathcal{A}_1] \leq n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*} Therefore, from \cref{cor:nazocor}, we have $f(A^{(\tau)})\geq m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$ (i.e.~$A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$) holds w.h.p.~for some $\tau=O(\log n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Corollary A.13 to reach $\mathcal A_2$.

nodes.name: Potential $f$
nodes.statement: Let $f(A)\mathrel{\mathop:}= \lfloor n\max\{|\beta_i|:i\in I_{>1}\}\rfloor$ and $m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$. We use \cref{cor:nazocor} to show $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$ for some $\tau=O(\log n)$. Here, we use $\mathcal{A}_1$ as $\mathcal{B}$ of \cref{cor:nazocor}. Note that $A\in\mathcal{A}_1$ implies $f(A)<m$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up Corollary A.13 with $\mathcal B=\mathcal A_1$.

nodes.name: Condition (1')
nodes.statement: From \cref{eqn:beta_sum_of_irv} and \ref{asm:asm2}, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[|\beta_i| \mid A]=\sum_{j\in[2]} u_{ij}^2 \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha_j \mid A]=\Omega(n^{-1})$. Here, note that, for every $i\in[2]$, there exists $j\in[2]$ such that $u_{ij}\neq 0$, since otherwise, it contradicts to the fact that the matrix $U$ is nonsingular. Thus, from \cref{cor:BEbound_cor}, it holds that, for any constant $h>0$, there exists a positive constant $C_1<1$ such that $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')< h\sqrt{n} \mid f(A)\leq m] < C_1.$ This verifies the condition~\ref{cond:nazo_sqrt} of \cref{cor:nazocor}.

nodes.name: Condition (2')
nodes.statement: Now we check the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff}. Let $z\in[2]$ be the least index satisfying $|\beta_z|=\max\{|\beta_i|:i\in[2]\}$. Suppose that $A\in \mathcal{A}_1$ satisfies $f(A)=\lfloor n|\beta_z|\rfloor \geq h\sqrt{n}$ for sufficiently large constant $h>\frac{100 C}{\epsilon_1}$ (recall that the constant $\epsilon_1$ is mentioned in \ref{asm:asm4}). Then, from \ref{asm:asm4}, we have \begin{align*} |\mathbf{E}[\beta'_z \mid A]| &\geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_z| + 0.01\epsilon_1|\beta_z|-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}} \geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_z|. \end{align*} Thus, from the Hoeffding inequality (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}), we obtain \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')<(1+0.98\epsilon_1)f(A) \mid A] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[f(A')<\frac{1+0.98\epsilon_1}{1+0.99\epsilon_1}\mathbf{E}[f(A')]\,\middle|\,A\right] \leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right) \end{align*} holds for every $A\in \mathcal{A}_1$ satisfying $f(A)\geq h\sqrt{n}$. This verifies the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff}.

nodes.name: Condition (3')
nodes.statement: Finally, we check the condition~\ref{cond:whp} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. From \ref{asm:asm5}, it holds that \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A'\not\in \mathcal{A}_1\text{ and }f(A')<m \mid A\in \mathcal{A}_1] \leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[\exists j\in I_{\leq 1},|\beta'_j|>\epsilon^* \mid A\in\mathcal{A}_1] \leq n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Reach $\mathcal A_2$
nodes.statement: Therefore, from \cref{cor:nazocor}, we have $f(A^{(\tau)})\geq m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$ (i.e.~$A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$) holds w.h.p.~for some $\tau=O(\log n)$.

nodes.name: Case II: $\mathcal A_2$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Case I\hspace{-.1em}I: $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{A}_2$.} Suppose that $A^{(0)}\in\mathcal{A}_2$ and let $j\in I_{>1}$ be the index satisfying $|\beta_j|>K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$. We remark that $K$ is sufficiently large. From \ref{asm:asm4} and \cref{eqn:beta'bounds}, we have $|\beta'_j|\geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_j|$. Thus, for some $\tau=O(\log n)$, we have $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j|>\epsilon^*$. Moreover, from \ref{asm:asm5}, we have $|\beta^{(\tau)}_i|\leq\epsilon^*$ for all $i\in I_{\leq 1}$. Therefore, $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_3$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric growth along an expanding direction reaches $\mathcal A_3$.

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A^{(0)}\in\mathcal{A}_2$ and let $j\in I_{>1}$ be the index satisfying $|\beta_j|>K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$. We remark that $K$ is sufficiently large.

nodes.name: Growth
nodes.statement: From \ref{asm:asm4} and \cref{eqn:beta'bounds}, we have $|\beta'_j|\geq (1+0.99\epsilon_1)|\beta_j|$. Thus, for some $\tau=O(\log n)$, we have $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j|>\epsilon^*$.

nodes.name: Reach $\mathcal A_3$
nodes.statement: Moreover, from \ref{asm:asm5}, we have $|\beta^{(\tau)}_i|\leq\epsilon^*$ for all $i\in I_{\leq 1}$. Therefore, $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{A}_3$ holds w.h.p.

nodes.name: Under Assumption 7.7
Eigenvalue gap
nodes.statement: Suppose that the fixed point $\mathbf{a}^*$ satisfies \cref{asm:escape_assumption2}. Let \begin{align*} I_{<1}&\mathrel{\mathop:}=\{i\in[2]:|\lambda_i|<1\}, \\ I_{>1}&\mathrel{\mathop:}=\{i\in[2]:|\lambda_i|>1\}. \end{align*} From \ref{asm:asm6}, we have $I_{<1}\cup I_{>1}=[2]$. Moreover, there exists some constant $\epsilon>0$ such that \begin{align} ||\lambda_i|-1| > 3\epsilon \end{align} holds for every $i\in [2]$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue gap $\epsilon$
nodes.statement: ||\lambda_i|-1| > 3\epsilon
nodes.label: eqn:epsdef

nodes.name: Regions $\mathcal B_i$
nodes.statement: For $A\subseteq V$, let $z=z(A)\in[2]$ be the least index satisfying $|\beta_z|=\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty$. We use four constants: In \cref{eqn:beta'bounds,eqn:epsdef}, we defined $C$ and $\epsilon$. Let $K\mathrel{\mathop:}=\frac{C}{\epsilon}$ and $\epsilon'\mathrel{\mathop:}= \frac{\epsilon}{C}$. Consider four events \begin{align*} \mathcal{B}_1&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}<\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon' \text{ and }z(A)\in I_{<1} \right\},\\ \mathcal{B}_2&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \right\}, \\ \mathcal{B}_3&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}<\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon' \text{ and }z(A)\in I_{>1} \right\}, \\ \mathcal{B}_4&=\left\{A\subseteq V\,:\, \|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty > \epsilon' \text{ and } |\beta_j|\leq \epsilon'\text{ for all }j\in I_{<1} \right\}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Claim
nodes.statement: We claim that, if $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{B}_i$, then $A^{(\tau)}\not \in \cup_{1\leq j\leq i}\mathcal{B}_{j}$ holds w.h.p.~for any $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ and some $\tau=O(\log n)$. This completes the proof of \cref{prop:escape} under \cref{asm:escape_assumption2}.
nodes.statement_short: From $\mathcal B_i$ the process leaves $\cup_{j\le i}\mathcal B_j$ in $O(\log n)$ steps.

nodes.name: Case I: $\mathcal B_1$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Case I: $A^{(0)}\in\mathcal{B}_1$.} Suppose $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{B}_1$. We argue that, if $A^{(t)}\in \mathcal{B}_1$, then either $A^{(t+1)}\in \mathcal{B}_3$ or $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t+1)}\|_\infty \leq (1-\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t)}\|_\infty$ holds w.h.p. For any $j\in I_{<1}$, the bound \cref{eqn:beta'bounds} yields that \begin{align*} |\beta'_j| &\leq (1-3\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty +C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_\infty + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq (1-\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty - 2\epsilon \|\beta\|_\infty + C\epsilon'\|\beta\|_\infty + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &= (1-\epsilon)\|\beta\|_\infty - \epsilon\|\beta\|_\infty + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq (1-\epsilon)\|\beta\|_\infty-(\epsilon K-C)\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq (1-\epsilon)\|\beta\|_\infty \end{align*} holds w.h.p. If $A^{(t+1)}\not\in\mathcal{B}_3$, then $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}'\|_\infty = |\beta'_j|$ for some $j\in I_{<1}$; thus, we have $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}'\|_\infty \leq (1-\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty$ w.h.p. Therefore, for some $\tau=O(\log n)$, either $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{B}_2$ or $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{B}_{3}$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Contracting coordinate dominates; norm shrinks until $\mathcal B_2$ or $\mathcal B_3$.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: Suppose $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{B}_1$. We argue that, if $A^{(t)}\in \mathcal{B}_1$, then either $A^{(t+1)}\in \mathcal{B}_3$ or $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t+1)}\|_\infty \leq (1-\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t)}\|_\infty$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Either enter $\mathcal B_3$ or shrink by $1-\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Contraction
nodes.statement: For any $j\in I_{<1}$, the bound \cref{eqn:beta'bounds} yields that \begin{align*} |\beta'_j| &\leq (1-3\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty +C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_\infty + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq (1-\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty - 2\epsilon \|\beta\|_\infty + C\epsilon'\|\beta\|_\infty + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &= (1-\epsilon)\|\beta\|_\infty - \epsilon\|\beta\|_\infty + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq (1-\epsilon)\|\beta\|_\infty-(\epsilon K-C)\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq (1-\epsilon)\|\beta\|_\infty \end{align*} holds w.h.p.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: If $A^{(t+1)}\not\in\mathcal{B}_3$, then $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}'\|_\infty = |\beta'_j|$ for some $j\in I_{<1}$; thus, we have $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}'\|_\infty \leq (1-\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty$ w.h.p. Therefore, for some $\tau=O(\log n)$, either $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{B}_2$ or $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{B}_{3}$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_short: Reach $\mathcal B_2$ or $\mathcal B_3$ in $O(\log n)$ steps.

nodes.name: Case II: $\mathcal B_2$
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry breaking via Lemma 9.3 and Corollary A.13.

nodes.name: Lemma 9.3
nodes.statement: Suppose $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{B}_2$. Our strategy is to apply \cref{cor:nazocor}. We will prove the following result in the last part of this subsection. \begin{lemma} Conditioned on $A\in \mathcal{B}_2$, the followings hold w.h.p.: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For every $i\in I_{<1}$, it holds that $|\beta'_i|\leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$. \item there exists a constant $h>0$ such that, for every $i\in I_{>1}$, \begin{align*} \left|\mathbf{E}\left[\beta'_i\,\middle|\,A,|\beta_i|\geq \frac{h}{\sqrt{n}}\right]\right| \geq (1+\epsilon) |\beta_i|. \end{align*} \end{enumerate} \end{lemma}

nodes.name: Bounds on $\beta'$ in the central region $\mathcal{B}_2$
nodes.statement: Conditioned on $A\in \mathcal{B}_2$, the followings hold w.h.p.: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For every $i\in I_{<1}$, it holds that $|\beta'_i|\leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$. \item there exists a constant $h>0$ such that, for every $i\in I_{>1}$, \begin{align*} \left|\mathbf{E}\left[\beta'_i\,\middle|\,A,|\beta_i|\geq \frac{h}{\sqrt{n}}\right]\right| \geq (1+\epsilon) |\beta_i|. \end{align*} \end{enumerate}
conclusions: the followings hold w.h.p.:
nodes.label: lem:beta'bounds

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Let $m=K\sqrt{n\log n}$ and define $f(A)\mathrel{\mathop:}=\left\lfloor n\cdot \max_{i\in I_{>1}}|\beta_i| \right\rfloor$. Suppose that $f(A^{(\tau)}) \geq K\sqrt{n\log n} $ holds w.h.p.~for some $\tau=O(\log n)$. Then, we have $A^{(\tau)}\not\in\mathcal{B}_1\cup\mathcal{B}_2$ w.h.p.~since $|\beta_i^{(\tau)}|\leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ holds w.h.p.~for any $i\in I_{< 1}$. Here, we used \ref{state:small} of \cref{lem:beta'bounds}. To show $f(A^{(\tau)}) \geq K\sqrt{n\log n}$, we check the condition \ref{cond:nazo_sqrt} to \ref{cond:whp} of \cref{cor:nazocor} and then apply it.

nodes.name: Condition (1')
nodes.statement: First, we check the condition~\ref{cond:nazo_sqrt} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. We use the same argument described in the Case I in \cref{sec:derivethm2.11fromasm2.9}. From \cref{eqn:beta_sum_of_irv}, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\beta'_i \mid A]\geq \sum_{j=1}^2 u_{ij}^2 \mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\alpha'_j \mid A]$. Moreover, for every $i\in[2]$ there exists $j\in[2]$ such that $u_{ij}\neq 0$, since otherwise, it contradicts to the fact that $U$ is nonsingular. From \ref{asm:asm2}, we have $\mathop{\mathbf{Var}}[\beta'_i \mid A]=\Omega(n^{-1})$; thus, from \cref{cor:BEbound_cor}, it holds that, for any constant $h>0$, there exists a positive constant $C_1<1$ such that $\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[f(A')\geq h\sqrt{n} \mid f(A)\leq m] < C_1$.

nodes.name: Condition (2')
nodes.statement: We check the condition~\ref{cond:chernoff} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. For every $i\in I_{>1}$, \cref{lem:beta'bounds} yields \begin{align} |\mathbf{E}[\beta^{(t+1)}_i \mid A^{(t)}\in\mathcal{B}_2]| \geq (1+\epsilon) |\beta^{(t)}_i|. \end{align} In look at \cref{eqn:beta_sum_of_irv}, from the Hoeffding inequality (\cref{lem:Hoeffding}), it holds for any set $A^{(t)}\in\mathcal{B}_2$, any index $i\in I_{>1}$ and any constant $\epsilon'>0$ that \begin{align} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[|\beta'_i| \leq (1-\epsilon')|\mathbf{E}[\beta_i']|]&\leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\epsilon'^2\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]^2n\right)\right) \leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\epsilon'^2\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right). \end{align} From \cref{eqn:beta_expect,eqn:beta_hoeffding}, by letting $\epsilon'=\frac{\epsilon}{2(1+\epsilon)}$, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|\beta^{(t+1)}_i| \leq \left(1+\frac{\epsilon}{2}\right)\cdot |\beta^{(t)}_i| \,\middle|\,A^{(t)}\in \mathcal{B}_2\right] &\leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[|\beta'_i| \leq (1-\epsilon') \cdot |\mathbf{E}[\beta_i' \mid A^{(t)}\in\mathcal{B}_2] |\right]\\ &\leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right). \end{align*} In other words, for any $A\in\mathcal{B}_2$ satisfying $f(A)\geq h\sqrt{n}$ for some constant $h>0$, we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[f(A^{(t+1)})<\left(1+\frac{\epsilon}{2}\right)f(A^{(t)})\,\middle|\,A^{(t)}=A \right]\leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Expected growth of $\beta_i$ on $\mathcal B_2$
nodes.statement: |\mathbf{E}[\beta^{(t+1)}_i \mid A^{(t)}\in\mathcal{B}_2]| \geq (1+\epsilon) |\beta^{(t)}_i|.
nodes.label: eqn:beta_expect

nodes.name: Hoeffding bound for $\beta'_i$
nodes.statement: \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[|\beta'_i| \leq (1-\epsilon')|\mathbf{E}[\beta_i']|]&\leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\epsilon'^2\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]^2n\right)\right) \leq \exp\left(-\Omega\left(\epsilon'^2\frac{f(A)^2}{n}\right)\right).
nodes.label: eqn:beta_hoeffding

nodes.name: Condition (3')
nodes.statement: Finally, we check the condition~\ref{cond:whp} of \cref{cor:nazocor}. From \cref{lem:beta'bounds}, we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}[A^{(t+1)}\not\in \mathcal{B}_2 \land f(A^{(t+1)})\leq m \mid A^{(t)}\in\mathcal{B}_2] &\leq \mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\exists j\in I_{<1}:\,|\beta'_j|> K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\,\middle|\,A\in\mathcal{B}_2\right] \\ &\leq n^{-\Omega(1)}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Apply Corollary A.13
nodes.statement: Now we are ready to apply \cref{cor:nazocor}. Thus, there exists $\tau=O(\log n)$ such that $f(A^{(\tau)})\geq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ and $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j| \leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ hold w.h.p.~for every $j\in I_{<1}$. Consequently, $A^{(\tau)}\in \mathcal{B}_3 \cup \mathcal{B}_4$ holds w.h.p.

nodes.name: Case III: $\mathcal B_3$
nodes.statement: \paragraph*{Case I\hspace{-.1em}I\hspace{-.1em}I: $A^{(0)}\in\mathcal{B}_3$.} Suppose that $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{B}_3$. From \cref{eqn:beta'bounds}, it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |\beta'_z|&\geq |\lambda_z||\beta_z|-C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty - C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\geq (1+\epsilon)|\beta_z| + (\epsilon|\beta_z|-C|\beta_z|^2)+\left(\epsilon|\beta_z|-C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right) \\ &\geq (1+\epsilon)|\beta_z|. \end{align*} Moreover, for any $j\in I_{<1}$, it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |\beta'_j| \leq (1-3\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty + C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_{\infty} + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \leq (1-\epsilon)|\beta_z| \end{align*} These imply that $A^{(t+1)}\not\in\mathcal{B}_1 \cup \mathcal{B}_2$ holds w.h.p.~whenever $A^{(t)}\in \mathcal{B}_3$. Let $\tau$ be the stopping time given by $\tau \mathrel{\mathop:}= \min\{t\,:\,A^{(t)}\not\in \mathcal{B}_3\}$. Then, $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t+1)}\|_\infty \geq (1+\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t)}\|_\infty $ holds w.h.p.~for all $t<\tau$. Therefore, we have $A^{(\tau)}\in\mathcal{B}_4$ with $\tau=O(\log n)$, and $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j|\leq \epsilon'$ for all $j\in I_{<1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Expanding coordinate grows by $1+\epsilon$ until $\mathcal B_4$.

nodes.name: Growth
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A^{(0)}\in \mathcal{B}_3$. From \cref{eqn:beta'bounds}, it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |\beta'_z|&\geq |\lambda_z||\beta_z|-C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty - C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\geq (1+\epsilon)|\beta_z| + (\epsilon|\beta_z|-C|\beta_z|^2)+\left(\epsilon|\beta_z|-C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right) \\ &\geq (1+\epsilon)|\beta_z|. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Contracting coordinates
nodes.statement: Moreover, for any $j\in I_{<1}$, it holds w.h.p.~that \begin{align*} |\beta'_j| \leq (1-3\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty + C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_{\infty} + C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \leq (1-\epsilon)|\beta_z| \end{align*} These imply that $A^{(t+1)}\not\in\mathcal{B}_1 \cup \mathcal{B}_2$ holds w.h.p.~whenever $A^{(t)}\in \mathcal{B}_3$.

nodes.name: Reach $\mathcal B_4$
nodes.statement: Let $\tau$ be the stopping time given by $\tau \mathrel{\mathop:}= \min\{t\,:\,A^{(t)}\not\in \mathcal{B}_3\}$. Then, $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t+1)}\|_\infty \geq (1+\epsilon)\|{\boldsymbol \beta}^{(t)}\|_\infty $ holds w.h.p.~for all $t<\tau$. Therefore, we have $A^{(\tau)}\in\mathcal{B}_4$ with $\tau=O(\log n)$, and $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j|\leq \epsilon'$ for all $j\in I_{<1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.3
nodes.statement: Suppose $A\in\mathcal{B}_2$ and recall the definition $K=\frac{C}{\epsilon}$. For any $i\in I_{<1}$, the bound \cref{eqn:beta'bounds} yields that \begin{align*} |\beta'_i|&\leq (1-3\varepsilon)K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}+K^2\frac{\log n}{n}+ C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq \frac{C}{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} - 2C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} + K^2\frac{\log n}{n} \\ &\leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \end{align*} holds w.h.p. This completes the proof of the statement \ref{state:small}. Now we consider the statement \ref{state:large}. Suppose that $A\in\mathcal{B}_2$ and $|\beta_i|\geq \frac{C}{\epsilon}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ (we expect $h=\frac{C}{\epsilon}$). For $i\in I_{>1}$, the bound \cref{eqn:exp_beta'} implies $|\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq |\lambda_i||\beta_i| - C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_{\infty} - \frac{C}{\sqrt{n}}$. Since $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ and $|\beta_i|\geq \frac{h}{\sqrt{n}}= \frac{C}{\epsilon}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, we have \begin{align*} &C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_{\infty} \leq \frac{CK\log n}{n}\leq \epsilon|\beta_i| \,\,\,\,\text{(for sufficiently large $n$)},\\ &\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}}\leq \epsilon|\beta_i|. \end{align*} This leads to $|\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq (1+\epsilon)|\beta_i|$, which completes the proof of the statement \ref{state:large}.
nodes.statement_short: Plug the bounds (47) and (46) into the definition of $\mathcal B_2$ with $K=C/\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Statement (i)
nodes.statement: Suppose $A\in\mathcal{B}_2$ and recall the definition $K=\frac{C}{\epsilon}$. For any $i\in I_{<1}$, the bound \cref{eqn:beta'bounds} yields that \begin{align*} |\beta'_i|&\leq (1-3\varepsilon)K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}+K^2\frac{\log n}{n}+ C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \\ &\leq \frac{C}{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} - 2C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} + K^2\frac{\log n}{n} \\ &\leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}} \end{align*} holds w.h.p. This completes the proof of the statement \ref{state:small}.

nodes.name: Statement (ii)
nodes.statement: Now we consider the statement \ref{state:large}. Suppose that $A\in\mathcal{B}_2$ and $|\beta_i|\geq \frac{C}{\epsilon}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ (we expect $h=\frac{C}{\epsilon}$). For $i\in I_{>1}$, the bound \cref{eqn:exp_beta'} implies $|\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq |\lambda_i||\beta_i| - C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_{\infty} - \frac{C}{\sqrt{n}}$. Since $\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|_\infty \leq K\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ and $|\beta_i|\geq \frac{h}{\sqrt{n}}= \frac{C}{\epsilon}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$, we have \begin{align*} &C\|{\boldsymbol \beta}\|^2_{\infty} \leq \frac{CK\log n}{n}\leq \epsilon|\beta_i| \,\,\,\,\text{(for sufficiently large $n$)},\\ &\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}}\leq \epsilon|\beta_i|. \end{align*} This leads to $|\mathbf{E}[\beta'_i]|\geq (1+\epsilon)|\beta_i|$, which completes the proof of the statement \ref{state:large}.
nodes.statement_short: Expanding coordinates grow by $1+\epsilon$ in expectation.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 10.2
nodes.statement: If $u=1$, the dynamical system given in \cref{eqn:2Cvecfielddef} is the same as that of the Best-of-three of \cref{eqn:3Mvecfielddef} and thus we are done. Suppose that $0\leq u<1$. The proof of this case depends on several results presented in \cref{sec:competitive_system}. We first claim that the map $T:S\to S$ is competitive (see \cref{sec:competitive_system} for definition). Then, we apply \cref{thm:orbit_convergence} and complete the proof of the first statement. To this end, we verify that the map $T$ satisfies the conditions \ref{cond:map_condition1} to \ref{cond:map_condition4} described in \cref{sec:competitive_system}. The condition~\ref{cond:map_condition1} follows from \cref{lem:criterion_C1}: it is straightforward to check that the Jacobian matrix \cref{eqn:general_Jacobian_2C} satisfies the condition of \cref{lem:criterion_C1}. We use the Inverse Function Theorem (\cref{thm:IFT}) to verify the condition \ref{cond:map_condition2}. To this end, we claim that $\det J>0$ for any $\mathbf{d}\in S\setminus\{(0,1)\}$. In view of \cref{eqn:general_Jacobian_2C}, let \begin{align*} f(d_1,d_2) &\mathrel{\mathop:}= \det J \\ &= \frac{1}{4}((2u+1-3u^2d_1^2-(2u+1)d_2^2)(3-u(2+u)d_1^2-3d_2^2)-4u(u+2)(2u+1)d_1^2d_2^2) \\ &\geq f(d_1,1-d_1) = \frac{1}{4}d_1^2(-1+u)\cdot h(d_1), \end{align*} where $h(\theta)\mathrel{\mathop:}= 3(-1+u)(1+u)^2\theta^2 + 12(1+u)^2\theta - 4(3+7u+2u^2)$. A simple calculation yields $h'(\theta) = 6(2-(1-u)\theta)(1+u)^2>0$ for $\theta\in[0,1]$ and thus \begin{align*} h(\theta)\leq h(1)=-3(1-u^3)-7u(1-u) < 0. \end{align*} Here, recall that $u<1$. Therefore, if $d_1>0$, we have \begin{align*} \det J &= f(d_1,d_2) \geq f(d_1,1-d_1) = \frac{1}{4}d_1^2(-1+u)h(d_1) >0. \end{align*} It is straightforward to see that $f(0,d_2)=0$ if and only if $d_2=1$. In other words, we have \begin{align} \det J =f(d_1,d_2)>0 . \end{align} for any $(d_1,d_2)\in S\setminus \{(0,1)\}$. Consequently, for any $\mathbf{d}\in S\setminus \{(0,1)\}$, an inverse mapping $T^{-1}(\mathbf{d})$ is defined. Moreover, it is straightforward to check that $T(\mathbf{x})=(0,1)$ if and only if $\mathbf{x}=(0,1)$. Therefore, $T$ is injective and we verified the condition~\ref{cond:map_condition2}. The condition~\ref{cond:map_condition3} follows immediately since we already have the Jacobian matrix \cref{eqn:general_Jacobian_2C}. To condition~\ref{cond:map_condition4} follows from \cref{lem:criterion_C4} and \cref{eqn:positive_det_2C}. Now we apply \cref{thm:orbit_convergence} and complete the proof of the first claim of \cref{prop:2Cvectorfield}. To obtain the second claim, we show that $d'_2>0$ whenever $(d_1,d_2)\in S$ satisfies $d_2>0$. This follows from a simple calculation \begin{align*} d'_2 &\geq \frac{d_2}{2}(3-3d_1^2-d_2^2) \geq \frac{d_2}{2}(3-3d_1-d_2) \geq d_2^2 >0. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: As for the Best-of-three: verify (C1)-(C4) for $T$ (determinant positivity via a one-variable polynomial bound) and apply the competitive-map convergence theorem.
